Full description:
Cameron Hunt brings 17 years of wealth management experience to his work with individuals and families. Earlier in his career, he worked in institutional portfolio construction and research, building, managing, and stress-testing portfolios across different market environments. Over time, he became increasingly interested in applying that analytical background directly to the financial decisions people make in their everyday lives.

Today, Cameron works with high-earning professionals and executives, including people managing RSUs, stock options, concentrated equity positions, and liquidity events. His planning work also spans retirement, tax planning, portfolio construction, cash flow, estate considerations, real estate, and alternative investments.

Cameron holds the CFA®, CFP®, and CPWA® designations. He combines the analytical perspective of his investment background with a broader planning process that considers how money connects to time, personal choice, health, meaning, and legacy. His goal is to help clients evaluate their resources in the context of the life they want to build.

Cameron also brings a practical understanding of marketing, particularly from the perspective of a self-directed advisor. That mindset complements his preference for clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and giving clients a framework they can understand and use.

Cameron and his wife are raising four young children in Central Oregon. His own experience balancing career ambitions, family life, and long-term planning influences how he thinks about wealth. For Cameron, financial planning is not only about accumulating assets. It is also about creating greater flexibility for family, experiences, and the choices that matter over time.

Full description:
My path to wealth management was shaped by real-world experience long before formal credentials. However, those formal credentials along with over 20 years of experience spearheaded my expertise and proficiency to work with high net worth individuals, families, and institutions.

I am a graduate of Texas Tech University and hold the Certified Investment Management Analyst® certification administered by the Investments and Wealth Institute and taught in conjunction with The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania. CIMA certification is the peak international, technical portfolio construction program for investment consultants, financial advisors, and wealth management professionals, and it stands out among other financial certifications for its effective emphasis on the combination of theory and practical application.

In addition, I hold the Certified Private Wealth Advisor® designation taught in conjunction with the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. The CPWA program takes a holistic and multidisciplinary approach that includes a deep dive into sophisticated wealth strategies, estate planning, wealth transfer, behavioral finance, family dynamics, tax management, and legacy planning. CPWA® certified professionals are able to identify and analyze the unique challenges high-net-worth individuals face and understand how to develop specific strategies to minimize taxes, monetize and protect assets, maximize growth, and transfer wealth.

Name: Chris Stennett
Intro description:
Hello 👋🏼 I’m Chris. I focus on building long-term, client-centered relationships by helping individuals and families navigate their financial journey with clarity and confidence. My approach centers on understanding each client’s unique goals, whether that’s planning for retirement, managing investments, or creating strategies for wealth transfer.

I believe trust is built through transparency and collaboration. By actively listening and tailoring strategies to each client’s circumstances, I aim to simplify complex financial decisions and provide solutions that empower clients to move forward with confidence.

Full description:
Chris Stennett is a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ practitioner with a genuine passion for helping individuals and families achieve financial freedom. His approach centers on education and empowerment, guiding clients through the complexities of personal finance so they can make confident, informed decisions that align with their goals. Chris believes financial planning isn’t just about building wealth—it’s about creating clarity and peace of mind for every stage of life.

As a life-long learner, Chris is constantly expanding his knowledge, often tuning into financial planning podcasts to stay on top of industry trends. While he jokes that it might sound boring, Chris’s clients quickly recognize the dedication behind it: a commitment to always bringing fresh ideas and strategies to the table.

At the heart of his work is a deep focus on relationships. Chris takes the time to truly understand each client’s unique story, values, and goals, building personalized plans that evolve as life does. Whether it’s designing retirement income strategies, guiding families through tax-smart investing, or simplifying complex planning decisions, he strives to make financial advice approachable, clear, and tailored.

Outside the office, Chris is proud to be a husband to his wife, Emily, and a father to two young daughters, Scarlett and Ivy, who keep life full of joy and perspective. An avid (though self-proclaimed “average”) golfer, he dreams of playing at the world’s best courses and enjoys connecting with clients over a shared love of the game.
Faq answer 1: I became a financial advisor in 2009, during the heart of the Great Financial Crisis, driven by a deeply personal mission. Growing up in a family that didn’t understand money and investing, I saw firsthand how a lack of financial knowledge could lead to a lifetime of insecurity. In college, after accumulating significant debt, I recognized I was following a similar path. I knew that I needed to change my relationship with money, and I wanted to help others who faced a similar struggle.
Faq answer 2: While I am happy to help anyone in need of financial planning, my practice primarily focuses on two client groups. The first are individuals in the mid-career and late-career stages of life who are preparing for retirement and seeking clarity around their long-term goals. The second are personal injury attorneys, who often face unique financial circumstances and benefit from specialized strategies tailored to their profession.
Faq answer 3: My expertise spans several key areas of wealth management, including financial planning, retirement planning, and tax optimization. I also specialize in business succession planning, cash-flow management, and estate and legacy planning. Whether it’s developing a roadmap for retirement, creating strategies to minimize taxes, or guiding business owners through succession planning, I focus on delivering comprehensive solutions that align with my clients’ long-term goals.
Faq answer 4: Clients, like fingerprints, are unique in terms of what they need to achieve financial success. Investment management is a critical component, but my role extends far beyond the portfolio: evaluating major financial decisions, navigating equity compensation and business ownership, planning taxes proactively, and coordinating with CPAs, estate attorneys, and insurance professionals so every piece of their financial life works together.

Like my clients, I'm a business owner making decisions about my own cash flow, family, and time, so the conversation is personal and practical, not theoretical.

Name: Christopher Ishack
Intro description:
Hi there! I’m Chris, a wealth advisor based in Orlando, Florida, with nearly two decades of experience helping individuals and families make thoughtful decisions around their investments, retirement, and broader financial lives. Throughout my career, I have developed a deep passion for helping clients turn complex situations into clear and disciplined strategies.

I work primarily with affluent and high-net-worth individuals and families, including professionals, executives, business owners, and people approaching or already in retirement. My approach starts with understanding what you are trying to accomplish, along with your tax situation, risk tolerance, income needs, liquidity needs, and personal preferences. From there, I build a tailored investment and financial planning strategy around the life you are working toward. Clients work directly with me, and I place a strong emphasis on being accessible when advice is needed and delivering a highly personalized experience.

Service description 4: We actively research alternative investment opportunities and monitor your portfolio investment holdings, bringing together actionable insights and forward-thinking risk assessments.
Full description:
Christopher Ishack brings 17 years of experience in financial services and wealth management to his work with clients. After earning his Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of Miami, he began his career at Northwestern Mutual. His early work introduced him to insurance, financial protection, investments, and comprehensive planning, and helped shape his interest in the investment side of wealth management.

While working full time, Christopher returned to the University of Miami to earn his MBA. After five years with Northwestern Mutual, he joined Bank of America and Merrill Lynch, where he spent the next 12 years working with individuals and families through changing markets and different stages of their financial lives.

Over the course of his career, Christopher developed a particular interest in helping clients bring structure to financial decisions that can involve several moving parts. His work often includes investment and portfolio management, retirement income planning, tax-aware investing, concentrated stock positions, fixed-income strategies, direct indexing, tax-loss harvesting, and alternative investments. When a client’s needs involve tax or estate planning, he can also coordinate investment decisions with the client’s CPA and attorney.

Christopher places a strong emphasis on accessibility and communication. He wants clients to understand the reasoning behind their financial decisions and to feel comfortable reaching out when an important question comes up, rather than limiting conversations to scheduled reviews.

Born and raised on Long Island, New York, Christopher now calls Orlando, Florida home. Outside of work, he has maintained a passion for fitness and strength training for two decades. He also enjoys traveling, discovering new places, and spending time with the people closest to him.
Faq answer 1:
After earning my Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of Miami, I began my career with Northwestern Mutual. My role introduced me to insurance and financial protection, but it also gave me my first exposure to investments and comprehensive financial planning. I found myself increasingly interested in helping clients make broader financial decisions and understanding how their investments fit into the rest of their lives.

While working there, I returned to the University of Miami to earn my MBA. After five years with Northwestern Mutual, I joined Bank of America and Merrill Lynch, where I spent the next 12 years deepening my experience in investment management and working with clients through different market environments and stages of life.

What kept me in wealth management was seeing the value an advisor can provide when someone is facing an important decision. Whether a client is preparing for retirement, investing a lifetime of savings, navigating market volatility, or trying to make their finances more tax-efficient, I enjoy helping turn a complicated situation into a clear and disciplined strategy.
Faq answer 2:
I primarily work with affluent and high-net-worth individuals and families, particularly those approaching or already in retirement. My passion for helping clients navigate the transition into retirement with confidence and work towards achieving lasting financial freedom inspired me to earn the Chartered Retirement Planning Counselor (CRPC) designation, further deepening my expertise in retirement planning. I also work with professionals, executives, and business owners who have accumulated meaningful wealth.

Many clients come to me when their financial lives have become more complex and they want a more personalized and proactive approach to managing investments, creating retirement income, addressing taxes, and coordinating the different parts of their financial lives.
Faq answer 3:
Investment and portfolio management, retirement and income planning, and tax-aware investing are at the core of my practice. I also work extensively with concentrated stock positions, fixed-income strategies, direct indexing, tax-loss harvesting, and alternative investments.

I hold the Chartered Retirement Planning Counselor (CRPC) designation, and much of my work in Orlando is with clients approaching or already in retirement. When a situation involves tax or estate planning, I coordinate with the client's CPA and attorney to ensure investment decisions align with the broader financial plan.
Faq answer 4:
The strategy is always tailored to each client’s unique circumstances, but a few situations come up frequently.

A client may have accumulated a significant position in a single company’s stock. The goal is often to reduce that concentration without creating an unnecessary tax burden, which means diversifying in stages and timing it around the client’s broader tax picture.

Another client may be two or three years from retirement with a portfolio that was built primarily for growth and now needs to begin producing income. That work involves determining which accounts to draw from, in what order, and structuring the fixed-income strategy around when those assets will actually be needed.

For clients already in retirement, the focus is on creating greater confidence that their income can withstand different market environments while continuing to keep pace with inflation.

For clients with substantial unrealized taxable gains, the opportunity may be less about finding better investments and more about reducing tax drag. In those situations, strategies such as direct indexing and tax-loss harvesting are often worth evaluating.

Alternative investments may also play a role when a client’s circumstances, objectives, and preferences make them appropriate. In those cases, I look beyond traditional investments to identify differentiated, alpha-seeking strategies that complement their overall portfolio.

Whatever the strategy, I want every holding to serve a clear purpose. If it’s in the portfolio, the client should understand exactly why it’s there.
Faq answer 5:
The relationships. I enjoy becoming the person a client trusts when an important financial decision comes up. It is a privilege and an honor to be considered their “trusted advisor”.

Some of the most rewarding conversations begin with a situation that feels complicated or stressful. We work through the details together, identify the available choices, and create a clearer path forward. Over time, you get to know much more than a client’s portfolio. You learn about their family, priorities, and what they want their wealth to accomplish. Building those long-term relationships is the part of this profession I value most.
Faq answer 6:
I chose Savvy because it gives me access to modern technology, broad investment capabilities, and the infrastructure of a sophisticated wealth management practice while preserving the flexibility to provide clients with a highly personalized experience.

What I particularly value is that the technology works behind the scenes to help me operate more efficiently rather than getting between me and the client. That gives me more time to focus on providing advice, managing investments, and being available when clients need me.

Name: Clayton Johnson
Intro description:
Hi, I’m Clayton. I work with business owners and executives who have built meaningful wealth and are facing increasingly complex decisions around taxes, investments, estate planning, executive compensation, and business transitions.

My approach starts with the after-tax result. I look across a client’s full balance sheet and coordinate decisions around where assets are held, when gains are realized, how compensation is structured, and how planning connects with a client’s CPA and attorney. The goal is to bring clarity to complicated situations and create a coordinated financial plan that reflects what the client is trying to accomplish.
Quote: I plan around the after-tax result from the beginning, coordinating investment, tax, and estate decisions so clients can see how each part of their financial life works together.
Team description: Pillar Capital is an independent, fee-only wealth management practice for high-net-worth individuals, business owners, and families navigating major financial transitions — a business sale, a property exit, or a concentrated, highly appreciated position. We specialize in improving after-tax outcomes, drawing on a broad range of advanced tax, estate, and investment strategies grounded in empirical research. Our philosophy is simple: decisions should be driven by data, not emotion, and every strategy should be clear enough to explain in plain language.
Service eyebrow 1: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 1: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service eyebrow 2: PRESERVATION OF YOUR LEGACY
Service description 2: We focus on making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible, helping support the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Service description 3: We build portfolios on decades of peer-reviewed research instead of predictions about where markets are headed. That means broad global diversification, deliberate tilts toward the company characteristics research shows are rewarded over time, and low costs at every layer.
Service eyebrow 4: STRATEGIC PLANNING OF YOUR FINANCIAL AND NON-FINANCIAL COMPENSATION
Service description 4: We are here to guide you through your compensation negotiation, helping you secure a package that aligns with both your short-term needs and long-term goals.
Full description:
Clayton Johnson is a Wealth Advisor at Savvy with more than 10 years of experience helping business owners, executives, and affluent families navigate complex financial decisions. His work brings together tax planning, investment strategy, estate and wealth transfer planning, executive compensation, and broader financial planning.

Clayton has particular depth working with business owners through periods of growth, liquidity, and succession. He helps clients evaluate decisions across their entire balance sheet rather than treating taxes, investments, and estate considerations as separate conversations. His planning process places significant emphasis on the after-tax result and on coordinating decisions with a client’s other professionals.

Prior to joining Savvy, Clayton worked at Aerodigm Wealth and Squire Wealth Advisors, where he integrated tax and wealth planning for business owners and executives. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Business Management from Brigham Young University and is both a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® professional and a Certified Private Wealth Advisor®. He is a member of the Investments & Wealth Institute and serves on the board of the Utah Valley Estate Planning Council.

Outside of work, Clayton enjoys playing sports, with volleyball at the top of the list. He also enjoys traveling with his wife and three daughters and spending time serving in his community and church.

I primarily work with business owners and executives with approximately $5 million to $25 million or more in net worth. Many are approaching a liquidity event, working through a significant tax issue, or realizing that the tax, investment, and estate sides of their financial lives have not been coordinated in one place.

These clients are often very good at running businesses or building successful careers. My role is to help organize the financial complexity that comes with that success and create a more coordinated planning process.

I frequently help clients evaluate ordinary income mitigation, capital gains deferral and offset strategies, asset location, charitable structuring, and planning ahead of a business transaction.

The common thread is an emphasis on after-tax wealth. Rather than looking only at an investment return or one planning decision in isolation, I consider how the pieces work together and what the client may ultimately retain after taxes.

Name: Colin Farr
Intro description: Hi there! 👋🏼 I’m Colin. I enjoy taking the time to understand each client’s individual situation and creating strategies to help them meet their goals. It’s also important to me that my clients understand how their investments work and why their portfolio is set up in a certain manner. From crafting investment strategies to tax optimization, income planning, and preparing for milestones like retirement or college funding – I’m here to help.
Quote: I love spending time educating clients, whether they want all the details or just a high-level overview. I want to ensure that clients understand why they own certain investments, why their portfolio is set up in a certain manner.
Service description 1: Transition into your golden years with confidence, regardless of age. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans with confidence and peace of mind.
Service eyebrow 2: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 2: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service eyebrow 3: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 3: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to each client’s specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Full description:
Colin is originally from Northeast Ohio but made his way to Colorado for college and to follow his passion for the great outdoors. His career in finance began at Charles Schwab over 14 years ago, where he spent the last decade as a Financial Consultant, assisting high net worth individuals and families. Holding the title of Certified Financial Planner (CFP®), Colin thrives on nurturing enduring connections and aiding clients in reaching their financial aspirations. He has moved to Savvy to offer his clients a more tailored experience alongside our tech forward team.

Residing in Denver, he unwinds from work by indulging in activities such as hiking, camping, and mountain biking. Colin enjoys spending time outdoors with his wife, Sarah, their two children, and their dog, Oliver.
Faq answer 1:

During this time I also had a college roommate who was an economics major and they were glued to CNBC which sparked my interests in the markets. Through a family connection, I was introduced to a Schwab advisor and found similarities between my job and the advisor's role intriguing. This realization led me to pursue a career in advising. I started at Schwab in 2010 and worked my way up to an advisory position at a brand office by 2013. After more than a decade serving as an advisor, I wake up daily to look at the markets and stay involved with the trends to offer the up to date advice to my clients.

When I joined Savvy, I began a collaborative venture with my close friend, Michaela Sullivan, who is now my partner as we join forces to assist clients. While I continue to support my individual clients, I look forward to working with Michaela on future clients and supporting each other as we grow our business. I love working with the markets and Michaela is focused on financial planning and combined we want to help our clients achieve their goals.
Faq answer 2: I work with a diverse clientele, with a focus on those approaching or in retirement, often with portfolios exceeding $1 million. I believe in not only guiding my clients on portfolio and retirement strategies but also to building connections with their children. I offer advice not only on trust/estate planning but also on education planning for the next generation. It’s important to involve children in the process to help plan for their future.
Faq answer 3: I like to optimize my clients financial future with services like investment and income planning, retirement strategies, tax optimization, social security planning, and guidance through life transitions and liquidity events such as divorce, property or business sales, and inheritances.
Faq answer 4: Tailored investment strategies, personalized to individual client needs such as income planning, tax optimization, gifting, and college funding.
Faq answer 5: I enjoy being able to analyze a client’s situation and create strategies to help them meet their goals. It’s very rewarding to see good outcomes, watch a family evolve over time and show clients how powerful investing and planning can be.
Faq answer 6: Coming from a firm that had a lot of slow processes and archaic technology, I love how efficient and tech forward things are at Savvy. It’s great that Savvy really listens to advisor feedback and implements solutions to allow us to spend more time focusing on our clients.

Name: Conrad Levesque
Intro description:
Hi, I’m Conrad. I’m a financial advisor based in Marietta, Georgia and the founder of DELVR Wealth. I work with business owners, high-earning families, and legacy-minded individuals who want more than investment management alone. My approach centers on comprehensive financial planning, with a strong focus on tax optimization, business owner planning, and long-term legacy strategies.

Before becoming a financial advisor, I spent years working with tax clients and kept hearing questions that called for broader financial guidance. That experience shaped the way I work today. I help clients connect the dots across their business, personal finances, and long-term goals so they can make informed decisions and spend more time on what matters most to them.
Quote: I help clients simplify complex financial decisions by serving as a planning partner across their business, taxes, wealth, and legacy goals.
Service eyebrow 1: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 1: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 2: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 2: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service description 3: Whether it’s transferring assets to kids or grandkids, or maximizing your charitable donations, we have the expertise with complex strategies surrounding wealth transfer.
Service description 4: Building a successful business is an incredible feat, but what happens to your hard-earned legacy when you're ready to step down? We build strategic blueprints to help ensure the continued growth and success of your enterprise.
Full description:
Conrad Levesque is the founder of DELVR Wealth. He brings 10 years of wealth management experience, along with more than two decades of experience serving tax clients and advising on complex financial matters for individuals and business owners.

Conrad earned his Bachelor in Business Administration in Management and his Bachelor of Science in Accounting from Kennesaw State University. He later earned his Certified Public Accountant designation and expanded his background through work in tax and accounting, real estate development, business consulting, and financial auditing for the State of Georgia.

In 2017, Conrad expanded his practice to include consulting and financial planning services. Today, he is a Certified Financial Planner professional®  and also holds the Certified Exit Planning Advisor credential, which supports his work with business owners who want to understand, protect, and improve the value of their businesses as part of their overall net worth strategy. His professional affiliations include the AICPA and the Georgia Society of CPAs.

Outside of work, Conrad enjoys spending time with his wife, Chelsea, and their two daughters, Caroline and Carson. He is also an avid golfer and enjoys participating in charity tournaments that support local causes.

Faq answer 2: I primarily work with business owners, high-earning accumulator families, and legacy-minded individuals. Many of my clients are looking for a more coordinated approach that brings together business planning, tax strategy, wealth planning, and long-term family goals.
Faq answer 3: I draw on more than 20 years of experience serving tax clients, along with my work as a CPA, CFP®, and CEPA. A major area of focus is helping business owners understand and improve the value of their business while protecting that value within their overall financial picture. I also work closely with high-earning families on tax planning, cash flow, and long-term wealth decisions.
Faq answer 4: I often help business owners with value enhancement planning designed to strengthen and clarify the value of their business over time. I also help clients deploy excess cash in tax-aware ways that support long-term accumulation and flexibility. For legacy-minded individuals and families, I regularly work on charitable planning, Roth conversion strategies, and multi-generational planning.
Faq answer 5: I value being part of my clients’ lives in a meaningful way. Over time, you get to see both the milestones and the challenges, and that creates a relationship that goes beyond a typical service model. It is rewarding to see the impact of good planning and to know the work we do supports real decisions and real life.
Faq answer 6: Savvy gives me access to a modern platform that supports a more connected planning experience for clients. It helps streamline the advisory process so I can stay focused on delivering thoughtful guidance and coordinating the different pieces of a client’s financial life.

Name: Craig Austad
Intro description:
Hi 👋🏼 I’m Craig. I specialize in helping clients align their finances with their values, creating thoughtful strategies that can help reduce stress and elevate both personal and financial well-being. My goal is to help keep my clients focused on what truly matters to them.

Many of my clients are also part of the "sandwich generation," navigating the complex responsibilities of caring for aging parents, supporting children through college, and planning for their own retirement. With a clear financial strategy—especially one that includes a well-structured college planning process—education can feel more affordable, all while ensuring other financial priorities stay on track.
Quote: My approach with clients is simple; help them thrive in both their personal and financial lives
Service description 1: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Service eyebrow 2: MAXIMIZE YOUR FINANCIAL RESOURCES
Service description 2: We guide clients through the intricate financial aid process, helping them navigate its many challenges. By empowering families to make well-informed decisions when choosing colleges, we help them maximize their financial resources while attempting to avoid the burden of excessive student debt.
Service eyebrow 3: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 3: We aim to minimize the ambiguity of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Lead magnet title: Funding College, Preserving Wealth: A Late-Stage Planning Blueprint for Families
Lead magnet copy:
• Get “pre-approved” for college the same way you would a mortgage
  • Know your true Expected Family Contribution before award letters arrive
  • Evaluate every offer using the PEGS formula so you never pay $50k/year for a $40k job

Perfect for juniors, seniors, transfer students, or parents who just opened a college bill and thought “There has to be a better way.”
Full description:
Craig Austad has been in the financial services industry for over 25 years, and his passion lies in helping individuals take control of their finances. He has extensive experience working with clients and utilizes this knowledge to manage his practice. He wears many hats at the firm, but his most important job is helping his clients make sound decisions about their assets. He believes it is rewarding to develop effective strategies for his clients to help them achieve their goals.

Craig is a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ professional and takes his industry education seriously. He is also a Chartered Life Underwriter™ and proud member of the Financial Planning Association of Colorado. When not in the office, he can be found in the mountains skiing with his wife and two kids, getting together with friends and family, and enjoying all that Colorado has to offer.

A few years later, I joined a firm that managed one of the retirement plans for the City and County of Denver, further deepening my expertise. Eventually, I earned my CFP® designation and worked with a wealth management firm specializing in business owners. However, I realized I wanted more flexibility to truly serve my clients' needs. This led me to establish Flourish Financial Partners, where I could help clients thrive on their financial journeys.

My focus is on working with individuals who understand the value of partnering with a professional—delegating the complexities of financial planning and investment management to help enhance their lives and alleviate unnecessary stress.
Faq answer 3: Alongside retirement planning and tax-efficient strategies, I specialize in late-stage college planning. By guiding clients through the complexities of the financial aid process and its many components, I help them make more informed decisions when selecting colleges. This approach is designed to enable families to reduce the burden of excessive student loans while maximizing their financial resources.
Faq answer 4: Many of my clients belong to the "sandwich generation," juggling the demands of caring for aging parents, supporting children through college, and saving for their own retirement. Successfully managing this "triple threat" requires a well-thought-out strategy to help them stay on track with their financial goals. One of the most impactful steps we can take is to guide these clients through our comprehensive college planning process. This approach helps create a clear plan, helps make college feel more affordable, and ensures that education expenses are balanced with other important financial priorities.

Name: Dan Brady
Intro description:
Hi there 👋🏼 I'm Dan, an experienced professional with over 25 years in institutional trading and investing. My expertise lies in investment allocations, helping clients overcome financial challenges, and understanding their unique needs.

As a financial advisor, I prioritize building strong, trusting relationships through empathy, open dialogue, and a deep connection. Regardless of financial standing, I am dedicated to assisting clients in achieving their goals. Let's embark on this journey together!
Quote: As a financial advisor, I prioritize building strong, trusting relationships through empathy, open dialogue, and a deep connection.
Service eyebrow 1: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 1: End-to-end investment management including a focus on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing. My specialty is in helping clients invest in companies that align with their values, while still seeking to generate strong returns.
Service eyebrow 2: Take control of your financial future
Service description 2: Personalized wealth management helps our clients grow and protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service description 3: Prepare yourself for your financial journey and navigate towards a life that you may not have even imagined possible after divorce.
Full description:
Dan brings 25+ years of experience in financial services together with a wide depth of financial acumen and differentiated perspective given his prior experience as both an institutional trader and sales trader. This background enables him to help guide clients through the full spectrum of financial concerns. Having invested through the bull and bear markets, he understands the importance of the big picture and that times of uncertainty can often be times of opportunity. In today's environment of economic and political uncertainty, clients need a financial compass - an experienced and trusted advisor who can help them navigate toward their financial futures with greater confidence.

Dan works with a broad spectrum of clients, including professionals, private equity executives, small business owners, and other successful individuals and families. While each client has their own unique financial goals, they all have one thing in common: appreciating the value of advice from a trusted, experienced advisor who has been through decades of boom and bust cycles.

He currently lives in Rye, New York, with his wife, Christine, and their four children, Ella, Logan, Connor, and Charlie.
Faq answer 3:
With a background in institutional trading and investing and over 25 years of experience, I am an expert in investment allocation. Beyond technical expertise, I excel in addressing the emotional aspect of financial planning. My compassionate approach, particularly evident in assisting divorcees, underscores my commitment to guiding clients through the emotional components of their financial journeys.

On the flip side, my expertise lies in the emotional aspect. I've discovered that this is a business with two complementary dimensions. I'm there to guide my clients to whatever their goals may be like retirement, but I found that the emotional component of the business is just as important. Recently, I’ve started building a niche practice working with divorcees. Many of my female divorced clients, who may have never before taken charge of their finances, experience a mixture of fear, worry, and sometimes even trauma. It is during these moments that I have found my support to be invaluable. I reassure them that everything will be alright, offering the reassurance of having an experienced professional by their side, equipped to help them navigate towards a life they may not have even considered possible after divorce.
Faq answer 4:
My journey, marked by overcoming financial challenges after my parents' divorce and my mother's subsequent illness, forms the foundation of my unique client approach. My ability to empathize, educate, and connect intimately with clients sets me apart. My commitment to ensuring an open dialogue, regardless of the client's financial standing, fosters a strong, trusting relationship.

I think because of where I am in life, as a father and husband with four children, a mortgage, life insurance, and a will, I'm understanding of almost everybody's situation because I'm living it. I'm living it as well as my clients are living it and I think that connection is super important.I think there's a certain amount of intimacy that comes with being a financial advisor. I don't want any of my clients to be afraid to ask me a question or to tell me something that needs to be shared. That intimate connection is so important to make this a successful relationship between me and my client. And I think I am very good at crossing that bridge because I've been through all of it.

And that goes for a client that has $500,000 or $200,000 with me, all the way up to a client that has five or ten or north of $5 million with me. Everybody has the same fears. Everyone has the same worries, and everyone has the same goals. They all want to live a life that they are comfortable with.
Faq answer 6:
Savvy has been a wonderful experience. It's everything and more than I could have expected when coming over, especially the powerhouse tech part of the firm where we built platforms internally with the advisor's guidance. It's a team effort. So the tech team doesn't just build something because they thought it would be good, they built something excellent while working with the advisor hand in hand.

The support that we get operationally is the best I've ever had in the business. The leadership has been wonderful. The closeness of the group has been more than anything I could have expected. As I've said, Savvy is a place where everyone's pulling their oars in the same direction. We all have the same goals. There are no closed doors at Savvy. If there's a question or a concern, you know where to get the answer. It has been just a wonderful, wonderful experience so far. I couldn't be happier.

Name: Dan Perrino
Intro description: Hello there! 👋🏼 I'm Dan, originally from Chicago and now residing in Bellingham, Washington. My lifelong passion for finance and the stock market has driven my career path. After completing my studies in business administration, with a focus on finance and information systems at Fordham University, I embarked on my professional journey at a financial technology company. As my expertise grew, I transitioned into financial advising and eventually found my way to Merrill in Bellingham. Presently, as a member of Savvy Advisors, I utilize their tech resources to provide exceptional client service.
Quote: My approach revolves around a comprehensive understanding of clients' tax situations and estate plans. I encourage collaboration with their CPAs and estate planning attorneys to align our strategies seamlessly.
Service description 1: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re 100% prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Service eyebrow 2: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 2: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service description 3: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Full description:
Dan grew up in the Chicago area and developed a strong interest in the stock market. After completing his bachelor's degree in business administration with concentrations in finance and information systems from Fordham University's Gabelli School of Business in New York City, he embarked on his career at Eze Software Group, a financial technology company and electronic trading software. Starting in client service, Dan steadily progressed to consulting and implementation roles, where he directly interacted with traders, portfolio managers, and operations personnel at institutional trade desks.

During his time at Eze, Dan had the pleasure of meeting his wife, Jess. Together, they decided to relocate to Bellingham, Washington, to be closer to her family. This prompted Dan’s transition to Merrill, where he served as a financial advisor, gaining valuable experience before eventually taking on the responsibility of managing a local independent advisory office in Bellingham.

In 2022, Dan joined Savvy, drawn by their cutting-edge technology resources, which he viewed as a valuable opportunity to provide better client service. Dan’s specialization lies in assisting individuals in his community in achieving their retirement goals. For those approaching retirement, his focus is on implementing effective savings and contribution strategies. For those already in retirement, he prioritizes sustainable and tax-efficient income strategies. Collaborating closely with clients' tax professionals is crucial to ensure that his investment advice aligns seamlessly with their unique tax situations.

Hi, I'm Daniel. I'm a Managing Partner and Wealth Manager with Palladian Asset Management, based in Midlothian, VA. For more than 38 years, I've helped a select group of individuals and families preserve, manage, and transfer wealth through comprehensive financial planning, investment management, and estate planning.

My work starts with a thorough financial plan. From there, I design and manage portfolios on a discretionary basis, aligning each strategy with a client's goals, risk tolerance, and long-term priorities.
Quote: I help clients create, preserve, and transfer wealth through planning, portfolio design, and long-term guidance.
Team description: Palladian Asset Management was built around a simple idea: that a small number of families, served well, is the best way to do this work. We are advisors, fiduciaries, and long-term partners, not a sales channel.

Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Service description 4: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Full description:
Daniel F. Murphy works with a select group of clients, helping them create, preserve, and transfer wealth. His planning process starts with understanding each client's financial picture, family needs, and long-term goals. From there, he designs investment strategies that reflect each client's objectives and risk tolerance.

Dan began his career with Aetna Life and Annuity Company after graduating from college. After a series of roles with increasing responsibility, he joined Wachovia Securities in Richmond, Virginia in 2005. He later spent eight years with Wells Fargo Advisors, formerly Wachovia Securities, before joining Claris Financial at the end of 2012.

Outside of work, Dan is a longtime member of Rotary Club and has served as Scoutmaster and Assistant Scoutmaster of a Boy Scout troop in Midlothian for more than 20 years. He lives in New Kent, Virginia, with his wife, Monica. They have two sons, Brendan and Colin. When he is not in the office, Dan enjoys golf and live music.

Full description:
Prior to founding Deep Fork, LLC powered by Savvy Wealth, Dan served as a Senior Trust Investment Officer with Arvest Wealth Management. He focuses on helping individuals and institutions manage, and protect their wealth through a comprehensive approach to wealth management that includes asset allocation, investment strategy, and risk management.

Dan brings deep financial expertise and a friendly, thoughtful demeanor to every client relationship, consistently exercising prudent judgment and care on behalf of those he serves. His experience spans more than two decades in the investment industry, where he has worked with high-net-worth clients,managing investment strategies, and navigating complex financial decisions with clarity and discipline.

A fourth-generation Oklahoman, Dan earned his bachelor’s degree in history from Oklahoma State University and a master’s degree in business administration from Oklahoma City University. He has also completed all PhD coursework in financial planning at Texas Tech University. Dan is a Chartered Financial Analyst® (CFA®) charterholder and a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ professional.

Dan began his career in the investment industry in 1998 and operated his own investment firm from 2000 to 2012. From 2013 to 2017, he served as a finance instructor at Northeastern State University, teaching courses in investments and personal finance. More recently, he was the Director of Investments at a wealth management firm in Edmond, Oklahoma, where he oversaw investment portfolios for high-net-worth clients.

Dan is the Past President (2024–2025) and a Board Member of the  CFA Society Oklahoma and is actively involved in prison ministry through the Oklahoma Department of Corrections via Crossings Community Church in Oklahoma City.

Faq answer 4:
While I help clients with an array of different financial challenges, I have advised many clients on transactional strategies. An example of this is when a client has built their wealth entirely out of real estate. As they look to retire, they may not want to pay long-term capital gains on selling their properties, but wish to rid themselves of responsibilities they incurred during their active real estate careers. I work with clients to facilitate a tax deferral transaction, called a Section 1031 or a  Like Kind Exchange, where clients sell their properties, and then reinvest all proceeds into passive real estate investments called Delaware Statutory Trusts that are designed to accept such tax deferred transactions. By becoming a passive investor in this structure, there were no more capital calls, it can give someone complete indemnification of all liability, but they can be stood as direct owners of investment real estate where the tax advantages still benefit them throughout.

I also help clients by using a financial planning model called the Wealth “RETENTION” Process. RETENTION stands for real estate, estate planning, tax strategies, education, nontraditional approach, traditional world-class service, insurance risk management, opportunistic investing, and non-insurable protection strategies. While I tailor the Wealth Retention Process to you, not all of these items apply to everyone but we focus on protecting your level of wealth that you have worked so hard to achieve either through straight forward or creative tax mitigation, protection strategies, and estate planning.

Name: David L. Berkowitz
Intro description:
Hi, I’m David. I’ve spent 40 years in financial services — trading and research at a Soros-backed hedge fund, five years advising CEOs and boards at Stern Stewart & Co., and more than twenty years running my own firm, ValueAligned Partners, which I founded in 2002. I hold two degrees from Columbia: a BA in Economics from Columbia College and an MBA from Columbia Business School.

Today I work mainly with people 50 and older, retirees, and their families. I help them answer the questions that matter most at this stage: Do we have enough? How do we turn savings into income? And would the family be OK if something happened tomorrow? I coordinate the financial, tax, and estate pieces as wealth passes from one generation to the next.

My approach centers on education and direct ownership of individual companies — one advisory fee, no fund fees layered underneath. I want clients, and their families, to understand what they own, how each holding fits their plan, and why staying focused on the long term matters.
Quote: After 40 years in this business, I can tell you the biggest risk in most retirement plans isn’t the market. It’s that only one person understands the plan.
Team description:
ValueAligned Partners manages money and builds financial plans for individuals and families who want a direct understanding of their financial lives — people who ask questions and expect straight answers.

The practice puts investment management, retirement income, tax and estate coordination, and family preparedness in one seat, so nothing falls into the gap between your advisor, your attorney, and your CPA. Behind it sits Savvy’s technology platform, which handles the operations and gives every client one live view of their full picture — and gives me more hours for research and for you.

Through ongoing education and direct communication, clients — and their families — come to understand what they own, why they own it, and how the plan carries them.

Full description:
David L. Berkowitz is the founder and Chief Investment Officer of ValueAligned Partners. His career spans four decades across hedge fund trading, investment research, corporate finance consulting, and portfolio management.

After earning his B.A. in Economics from Columbia College, David began his career as an entrepreneur before joining Woodward & Associates, an equity hedge fund that managed approximately $250 million at the time. Because the organization was small, David served in several capacities, including trading, research, client service, accounting, and operations. He later became Chief Operating Officer and Head Trader.

David returned to Columbia University to earn his M.B.A. in Finance and Value Investing from Columbia Business School. After graduation, he joined Stern Stewart & Co., the consulting company associated with the development of Economic Value Added, or EVA. During his five years there, he advised businesses on valuation, corporate operations, financial decision-making, and shareholder value. He also taught corporate finance concepts to audiences ranging from executives and board members to employees without formal finance backgrounds.

In 2002, David launched his own investment business. What began as a hedge fund and a relationship with a family office developed into an advisory practice serving individuals and multigenerational families through separately managed accounts.

David created the ValueAligned Investing framework, which combines value investing with an evaluation of management decisions, shareholder alignment, returns on capital, competitive positioning, and share repurchases. Rather than relying on mutual funds, exchange-traded funds, or outside managers, David researches and selects individual companies for client portfolios.

A significant part of David’s work involves helping clients understand market behavior and remain focused during periods of uncertainty. He enjoys teaching clients about the businesses they own and discussing how investment decisions connect with retirement, taxes, estate planning, and family goals.

David also publishes investor education through Berk on Value across video, written articles, and LinkedIn. He has presented to professional organizations and educational audiences in several cities, as well as at Columbia Business School and other business forums.

Asignificant part of David’s work is teaching clients — and their families —what they own: in meetings, in writing, and through the free investor educationhe publishes weekly.
Faq answer 1:
I have been involved in finance for my entire adult life. After graduating from Columbia College with a degree in economics, I started a video-rental vending business in Florida. When that business did not gain the traction it needed, I sold the machines and moved to New York.

In 1989, I joined Woodward & Associates, an equity hedge fund that served as an outside manager for the Soros Fund. Because it was a small organization, I wore many hats. I worked as a trader, research analyst, client service representative, accountant, and operating executive. That experience taught me how markets behave in the short term and how businesses create value over much longer periods.

I later earned my M.B.A. from Columbia Business School and joined Stern Stewart & Co. There, I advised companies on shareholder value, valuation, corporate finance, and operations.

In 2002, I launched my own hedge fund. Friends and relatives also wanted access to my investment management, but many could not invest directly in the fund. I began managing their assets through separate accounts, and the financial advisory practice grew from there.

When the hedge fund closed, I continued managing portfolios and helping families connect their investments with financial, retirement, tax, and estate planning.
Faq answer 2:
I primarily work with people age 50 and older and their families.

Some clients are preparing for retirement and want to understand whether their savings, investments, and expected income can support the life they envision. Others are already retired and need help managing their assets, planning distributions, and making decisions as their circumstances change.

I also work with multigenerational families. This includes helping parents introduce their children to saving and investing, preparing family members to inherit assets, and coordinating financial decisions following the death of a loved one.
Faq answer 3:
My background includes investment research, equity analysis, stock trading, portfolio management, corporate governance, executive compensation, financial planning, and the coordination of tax and estate considerations.

As a former EVA consultant, I studied how businesses create or reduce shareholder value. That experience continues to shape how I evaluate companies today.

I also worked as a hedge fund accountant and portfolio manager, which gave me a detailed understanding of portfolio structure, security selection, and the tax consequences associated with investment decisions. I am not a tax professional, but I consider taxes when evaluating transactions and portfolio changes.
Faq answer 4:
I help clients connect retirement planning with long-term ownership of individual companies.

We generally look for quality businesses with strong returns on capital, durable competitive positions, thoughtful capital allocation, and management teams whose interests are aligned with shareholders. Rather than trading in response to short-term market movements, we seek to own companies for long periods.

This approach can give individual investors an advantage that many professional managers do not have. Families are not required to report quarterly results or respond to short-term performance pressure. When their financial plan, cash reserves, and risk capacity are properly considered, they may be able to hold investments through downturns and participate in later recoveries.

I also help clients evaluate retirement cash needs, taxable and retirement accounts, Roth conversions, capital gains, tax-loss opportunities, and the transfer of assets to heirs in coordination with their tax and legal professionals.
Faq answer 5:
My favorite part is working with multigenerational families.

I enjoy watching clients’ children grow, teaching younger family members how to save and invest, and helping families prepare for the financial transitions that occur throughout life.

It is especially rewarding when clients begin with limited knowledge of stocks or the markets and gradually develop a clear understanding of what they own. I enjoy seeing the moment when a complicated investment idea begins to make sense.

Over time, our conversations extend beyond portfolios. We discuss companies, the economy, retirement, family milestones, and the difficult decisions that follow the loss of a loved one. Being able to support families through those moments is one of the most meaningful parts of my work.
Faq answer 6:
I look forward to using Savvy’s technology and collaborative resources to strengthen the planning experience for my clients.

The platform provides tools for financial planning, organizing client information, tracking important priorities, and improving communication. Savvy’s interest in developing thoughtful workflows and using technology to support advisory relationships can help me spend more time educating clients and addressing the decisions that matter to their families.

Derek approaches his work in financial services with a focus on trust and believes in a strong work ethic. He is deeply committed to each client and strives to build a sense of personal connection as he supports their journey to success. His mission is to help clients achieve their financial goals.

Drew Martino, based in Calabasas, CA, is a dedicated financial advisor at Savvy Wealth. With over 20 years of experience in financial services, Drew's career began in credit and lending, where he optimized household balance sheets. The 2008 great recession profoundly impacted Drew, as he witnessed the severe consequences of inadequate financial planning on families. Motivated to make a difference, Drew transitioned to financial advising to help clients avoid such financial disruptions and secure their retirement plans through proper planning and risk mitigation. His journey reflects a deep commitment to ensuring that families achieve their financial goals.

In addition to his professional work, Drew is actively involved in his community. He volunteers as a youth baseball and football coach, sponsors underserved youth during Christmas, and teaches financial education to children in both private and public schools.

Full description:
Dustin Parsons, an Arkansas native, joined Savvy Wealth in December 2023 as a founding Principal Wealth Manager bringing more than fourteen years of financial industry experience including banking, lending, investment, retirement, insurance and estate planning. Rooted in his personal and professional experiences over the last two decades, Dustin has a passion for helping families, professionals, entrepreneurs, businesses and non-profit organizations to build, manage and protect their financial legacy. Dustin works with his clients to create complete financial plans including budgets with debt payoff and strategic cash flow strategies. He firmly believes that financial education and coaching should be accessible to everyone, from high net worth professionals to young families just getting started. Dustin prides himself on his ability to bring complex financial strategies down to anyone’s level of understanding.Becoming a licensed Financial Advisor in 2017, Dustin transitioned from personal banking to investment and retirement planning. He has helped hundreds of individuals in Arkansas and beyond reach their financial goals by delivering highly customized investment strategies and holistic financial planning. In his free time, Dustin enjoys spending quality time with family, playing music, traveling and enjoying the outdoors.

Education
Dustin holds a Bachelor of Science in Marketing with concentration in Communications from University of the Ozarks in Clarksville, AR. Additionally, Dustin holds his Series 7, Series 66, Life & Health Insurance licenses, Accredited Asset Management Specialist (AAMS™) designation from the College of Financial Planning and is certified in Lean Six Sigma.

Name: Dustin Roberts
Intro description:
Hi there! 👋🏼 I’m Dustin, a Wealth Manager based in the Central Valley of California, with experience and deep passion in helping clients navigate the complexities of wealth management. My focus is on crafting personalized financial strategies that align with each of my client’s unique goals, whether it’s investment management, estate planning, or optimizing private banking solutions. I take pride in building long-term relationships and providing a comprehensive approach to financial success.

Outside of work, I’m actively involved in my community and have served on the Board of Directors for Advancing Children of Turlock. I also love coaching youth soccer and helping young athletes grow both on and off the field. When I’m not working, you’ll find me woodworking, taking family trips in my motorhome, and perfecting my skills as a BBQ pitmaster!
Quote: Above all, client experience is my top priority. I pride myself on being readily available, offering a level of personal service that makes clients feel heard, supported, and confident in their financial future. I treat my clients like family, building relationships based on trust, transparency, and long-term partnership.
Service eyebrow 1: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 1: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 2: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING FOR AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 2: Personalized wealth management is aimed to help our clients grow and protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service description 3: We excel in assisting real estate investors with mapping out their financial futures, whether by developing exit strategies for property sales, facilitating pre-purchase property evaluations, or revealing hidden opportunities.
Service description 4: Building a successful business is an incredible feat, but what happens to your hard-earned legacy when you're ready to step down? We build strategic blueprints to help ensure the continued growth and success of your enterprise.
Full description:
Dustin began his career in the banking and financial services industry in 2008. Before joining U.S. Bank Private Wealth Management, he worked as a Wealth Relationship Manager at BBVA USA. His professional background includes personal and business financial planning, real estate and specialty lending, and developing customized financial solutions to meet clients' needs. His focus is on building long-term relationships with clients, helping guide them and crafting personalized financial strategies that align with each of their unique goals.

Dustin is an active member of his community, having served on the Board of Directors for Advancing Children of Turlock. He also enjoys giving back by coaching youth soccer, helping young athletes grow both on and off the field.

Dustin resides in the Central Valley of California but works with clients across the Los Angeles, San Diego, Bay Area, and Central California markets. When he’s not working, you can find Dustin woodworking, taking family trips in his motorhome, and perfecting his skills as a BBQ pitmaster.
Faq answer 1:
Seventeen years ago, I was recruited into banking as a Business Banker for a community bank. I loved working with business owners - learning their stories, understanding how they operated, and seeing firsthand how they generated revenue and planned for growth.

Being raised by parents who started a small business together, I really connected with small business owners. I understood their operations and capital needs, but I also noticed a significant gap, being that many lacked long-term financial planning. Most didn’t have investment or retirement accounts, and estate planning was often overlooked. Their business was their passion, and they poured everything into it, often at the expense of securing their financial future.

Recognizing this need, I expanded my expertise by working in personal and private banking with institutions like JP Morgan, BBVA, and U.S. Bank Private Wealth Management. In 2012, I became a financial advisor to help clients bridge these gaps. Rather than simply selling financial products, I take a comprehensive approach, diving deep into each client’s financial picture to build a true partnership. My goal is to ensure every client has clarity, confidence, and a solid plan in place.
Faq answer 2: I have the privilege of working with a diverse group of clients, including doctors, dentists, CPAs, attorneys, business owners, and real estate investors. My focus is on individuals who recognize the value of strategic financial planning and want expert guidance in building, protecting, and optimizing their wealth. Whether they’re navigating complex tax strategies, planning for retirement, or seeking to grow their investments, I provide tailored solutions designed to address the personalized needs of each client.
Faq answer 3: My expertise includes investment management, cash management strategies, and private wealth management. I work closely with clients to optimize their insurance coverage, enhance business operation efficiency, and develop tailored financial strategies that align with their long-term goals. Above all, I prioritize strong client relationships, ensuring that each individual or business I work with receives personalized guidance and a comprehensive approach on their journey to achieve financial success.
Faq answer 4:
My approach to financial strategy is comprehensive and tailored to each client’s unique situation. I call it financial trimming - kind of like a tree. For businesses, I conduct a full financial review, identifying opportunities to increase efficiency, reduce unnecessary costs, and optimize cash flow. This includes evaluating loans, lines of credit, and treasury management strategies to ensure businesses are operating as effectively as possible.

For personal clients, I take a holistic view of their financial landscape, reviewing bank and investment accounts to ensure alignment with their goals. I help clients strategically allocate funds, assess and update trust documents, and explore ways to enhance estate planning strategies for long-term family benefit. Many trusts become outdated over time, and I work closely with clients to ensure their estate plans reflect their current wishes and take advantage of available strategies.

My expertise also extends to personal and business lending, multi-family investments, SBA financing, commercial real estate, and home equity solutions.

Above all, client experience is my top priority. I pride myself on being readily available, offering a level of personal service that makes clients feel heard, supported, and confident in their financial future. I treat my clients like family, building relationships based on trust, transparency, and long-term partnership.
Faq answer 5: My favorite part of working with clients is that I get the honor and privilege to learn their story and see what is important to them. It is only after I truly learn what is important to a client before any recommendations are made. I love being the trusted advisor that people know they can come to. My clients all know that we are on the same team, and we will work together to accomplish their goals. When I provide true value to my clients, I get an overwhelming sense of joy, and I take that responsibility seriously.
Faq answer 6:
What continues to excite me most about working with Savvy is the firm’s commitment to innovation, independence, and client-first service. In my opinion and experience, too many traditional firms rely on outdated technology, making it frustrating for clients to access and manage their financial information. Savvy is committed to changing that by providing an all-in-one dashboard that offers a comprehensive view of a client’s financial picture.

I also value the freedom and flexibility Savvy provides. This independence enables me to focus solely on my clients’ needs, without pressure, without distractions, so I can build meaningful, long-term relationships and create strategies tailored to their success.

Name: Dustin Thomas
Intro description:
Hi, I’m Dustin. As a CFP® and CPA with over 24 years of experience, I help a select group of high-net-worth individuals maximize their wealth by focusing on their entire balance sheet—not just their investment portfolio.

Most wealth management occurs in a vacuum, but the tax code dictates that almost every financial decision has a tax impact. My clients rely on me to serve as their Personal CFO, providing the technical oversight and forward-looking projections necessary to avoid overpayment and unwelcome surprises.
Quote: My favorite part about working with clients is helping them envision what’s possible. Moving beyond the question of “Will we be okay?”, I take pride in mapping out their future—whether it’s empowering them to give more, spend more, and live more freely, or guiding them to make thoughtful adjustments to stay on track toward their goals.

Service description 4: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to each client’s specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation, along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Full description:
Dustin Thomas is a financial advisor at Savvy, serving clients throughout the Greater Indianapolis area and Noblesville. With over twenty-four years of experience in the financial industry, Dustin specializes in working with high-net-worth individuals, including:

Executives of public companies

Retirees

Physicians

Dustin's expertise bridges the gap between tax professionals and financial advisors, providing tax-efficient strategies for his clients. He is passionate about helping his clients plan for the future and develop close relationships with them.

Dustin holds the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and Certified Financial Planner™ (CFP®) designations. He is also a member of the Financial Planning Association (FPA).

In his free time, Dustin enjoys spending time with his wife, Annette, rooting for the Ohio State Buckeyes, playing golf, and traveling. He also volunteers with the Animal Protection League to help take care of adoptable cats and is a member of the Noblesville Rotary Club.

Name: Ed Wildermuth
Intro description:
Hi there! 👋🏼 I’m Ed, a financial advisor based in Westfield, Indiana. I began my career in financial services in 2012 after spending ten years in corporate accounting and finance. Today, I focus on helping the working affluent navigate all areas of financial planning, from investment management and benefits consulting to risk management and long-term strategies. I hold degrees in Accounting and Business Administration from Monmouth College, and I’m proud to be a CPA as well as a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® and Chartered Financial Consultant® (ChFC®). I also stay active in the profession by serving as Co-Director of NexGen for the Financial Planning Association’s Great Indiana Chapter, mentoring newer advisors.

Outside the office, I’m passionate about giving back. I’ve donated nine gallons of blood (and counting!), coordinate community blood drives with the Red Cross, and volunteer with my fraternity to mentor students at local universities on personal finance 101. At home, I enjoy spending time with my wife and our two daughters. You’ll often find me golfing, hitting CrossFit workouts at an unreasonable hour, smoking meat, or home brewing! I’m also a lifelong fan of the Cubs, Bears, and Bulls, no matter how far from Chicago I live.
Quote: Being a financial advisor isn’t just about numbers on a page. It’s about being there for people during the moments that shape their lives. Whether it’s celebrating a new baby, navigating a career change, or guiding a family through loss, I see my role as walking alongside my clients every step of the way. At the end of the day, I want them to feel confident, cared for, and supported, no matter what life throws their way.
