Full description:
Ed embarked on his financial services journey in 2012, following a decade-long stint in corporate accounting and finance. His experience lies in providing comprehensive financial planning to his clients, encompassing investment management, benefits consulting, risk management, and long-term strategies. Ed's clientele primarily consists of the working affluent, those who have high income with their assets steadily catching up.

Ed is a distinguished alumnus of Monmouth College in Monmouth, Illinois, where he graduated with honors in both accounting and business administration. In 2008, he earned the esteemed Certified Public Accountant (CPA) certification. Additionally, he further bolstered his credentials in 2019, by obtaining the Chartered Financial Consultant® (ChFC®) and CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® certifications. Ed also serves on the Great Indiana Chapter of the Financial Planning Association, serving as the Co-Director of NexGen, working with less experienced advisors to learn and succeed early on in their careers.

Beyond his professional endeavors, Ed is an avid blood donor, having donated an impressive nine gallons and counting. In 2017, he joined forces with the Red Cross and a local craft brewery to organize a community blood drive, assuming the role of blood drive coordinator. To date, this event has successfully collected over 100 units of blood. He also volunteers his time with a local chapter of his fraternity, mentoring their executive board on the chapter’s finances.

Ed currently resides in Westfield, Indiana, with his wife and two daughters. Despite his geographical distance, his unwavering loyalty remains with the Cubs, Bears, and Bulls. In his leisure time, you can find him golfing, CrossFit at unreasonable times in the morning, smoking meat, and home brewing. He might even share one of his homebrews with you!
Faq answer 1: The thought of becoming a financial advisor always intrigued me, but graduating right after 9/11 and coming from a family history of accountants, it was the logical route to go, especially when new jobs were hard to come by. Fast forward to 2010, and my wife and I wanted to relocate to another city before starting a family. We had both grown up in the Chicagoland area, and knew this was our best chance to see what else was out there. After several extended weekends to various cities, we knew that Nashville was the next place to call home. So from there, I found a new job and it took us down to Music City. In 2012, I got a large promotion and raise, but the passion and impact wasn't there. So after much research and a big leap of faith, I took the plunge into financial services. I knew that I could take the skills I already had and use them to make a difference I could see in the families I worked for, that’s what ultimately fuels me to show up for my clients everyday.
Faq answer 2: I work with a wider variety of clients who recognize that the financial world can be overwhelming to navigate on your own. My role is to be a trusted guide that can be by their side and help them achieve their goals. I help my clients cut through the noise, make confident decisions, and move toward their goals with a sense of clarity. At the end of the day, it’s not just about achieving those goals, but doing so in a way that feels easier, less stressful, and aligned with what truly matters to them.
Faq answer 3: Over time, I've developed a specialty in tax, and the Gen X/Y family. Taxes are all around us and are prevalent in so many decisions we make. My background helps clients avoid many pitfalls laid out and trap a lot of unsuspecting families. I have also found that Gen X and Y have all often been overlooked by the financial industry. So many of the toughest and most challenging financial decisions happen mid-career, while raising a family and often helping aging parents. These are the families that may not meet the minimum assets of a corporate organization, but need help with topics outside traditional investments and insurance. This is where I found a large need, and living through it myself with my own family, I can relate to their situation.
Faq answer 4: The strategies depend on the time of the year, as many topics are cyclical. Early in the year, my clients and I are working on new goals and buttoning up last year's taxes. In the spring, it's time for tax projections, and I deep dive into portfolios. The summer can be a little quieter, which is a great time for less time sensitive topics like reviewing home and auto insurance and estate plan documents, and beneficiary checkups. The fall brings benefits to open enrollment for many, and thinking of education planning and funding.  Closing out the year, the winter brings on tax efficient topics like Roth conversions, tax gain/loss harvesting, and charitable contributions.
Faq answer 5: It's humbling to know that I'm the call after many clients share good (and bad) news with their immediate family. Eric Hamberg has served as a financial advisor with Rik Saylor Financial since 2008 and became a co-owner of the practice in 2021. His work focuses on helping families and business owners understand complicated financial questions and make informed decisions around their goals.

A CFP® professional, Eric works across family financial planning, retirement planning, investment and asset management, tax analysis and planning, insurance considerations, estate planning coordination, and planning for small businesses. His approach is highly individualized. Rather than starting with a predetermined solution, he builds planning around what each client wants to accomplish.

Eric also collaborates with CPAs, attorneys, and other professionals when a client’s situation calls for coordinated guidance.

He earned a BBA in Finance and Real Estate from the University of Cincinnati and holds the Series 66 along with life, health, and annuity insurance licenses. Eric has also served Sweet Cheeks Diaper Bank in several capacities, including Treasurer from 2018 to 2020, Board Chair from 2020 to 2022, and Finance Committee member from 2018 to 2023. He was named to the Cincinnati Business Courier’s Forty Under 40 Class of 2023.

Eric and his wife, Autumn, live in West Chester, Ohio, with their four children, including two sets of twins. A second-generation Elder High School graduate and proud West-sider, he enjoys spending time outside with his family and fitting in a round of golf when he can.

From a young age, I've been driven to pursue a career as a financial advisor. Seeing close friends and family struggle with poor financial guidance and retirement challenges made me realize the immense impact of competent advice. This realization fueled my passion, even during high school, when I actively sought opportunities to learn more about this industry. Faq answer 2:
I work with clients across the nation, addressing a wide range of significant issues faced by individuals in their 50s, 60s, and 70s. This includes providing expertise in tax planning, wealth management, financial planning, estate planning, and optimizing social security benefits. Each client's situation is unique, requiring tailored solutions that align with their specific needs and goals.

However, it's important to note that not all clients fit into this category. I also serve as a transition specialist, assisting individuals who are undergoing significant life changes, such as transitioning into retirement, starting a nonprofit, embarking on their own business ventures or navigating the loss of a loved one. Additionally, I have experience working with clients who have experienced financial windfalls later in life.

My purpose is to understand what clients value most and help them make informed decisions on how to best utilize it. It's no longer solely about retirement; some individuals may have different aspirations and a desire to explore new opportunities. I take a personalized approach, offering guidance and carefully considering various options for their next chapter.
Faq answer 3:
Early on, it became apparent to me that there was a need beyond a sole focus on investments for a holistic approach to financial advising. While I still do investment planning I like to look at the bigger picture of a client's financial health. Over time, I have honed my expertise in tax planning, estate planning, Social Security timing, and a comprehensive assessment of individual circumstances—beyond just a client's portfolio. Tax considerations play a significant role in a portfolio, but other aspects come into play as well.

While I provide guidance on various types of insurance, such as life, long-term care, and disability, I emphasize the importance of consulting an insurance professional once we identify areas for improvement. This process involves working closely with my clients on an annual basis, reviewing their property and casualty insurance. Cash flow budgeting and income distribution represent critical aspects that are often overlooked. Transitioning from asset accumulation to de-cumulation requires careful consideration of creating a retirement paycheck. Determining the optimal amount and method to withdraw funds, considering their financial plan, cost efficiency, and tax implications, is pivotal. This process involves a comprehensive analysis and exploration of the most suitable accounts and vehicles. It is not a mere exercise of throwing numbers around—it requires a thorough understanding of each individual's unique circumstances.
Faq answer 4:
There are numerous types of strategies to consider depending on the clients, but recently I did a financial plan for a couple in their early to mid-sixties who plan to retire within the next one to two years. This is a great example because retirement planning can happen at any point, it’s never too late or too early to plan for retirement. It was crucial to have a conversation with them before their retirement, as it gives us time to make necessary adjustments. During a comprehensive review of their situation, I discovered many areas that needed attention.

Firstly, their home insurance coverage was inadequate, especially considering the possibility of natural disasters causing significant damage. They had recently completed a major remodel, which their insurance didn't account for. Additionally, they didn't have sufficient umbrella insurance to protect them.

I also delved into their tax returns and found opportunities for optimization. Although they were generous in their charitable contributions, we helped them establish a more efficient and strategic approach to maximize the impact of their donations. Furthermore, I realized their estate plan didn't align with their desired legacy goals of leaving money to both charities and their children.

Name: Eric Passin
Intro description: Hi there! 👋🏼 I'm Eric, a financial advisor from Northern New Jersey with a creative approach to wealth management, influenced by my background in a family of artists and designers. I’m passionate about educating clients and empowering them to make informed financial decisions. From retirement planning to tax-efficient strategies, I focus on providing personalized advice that helps families achieve lasting financial security. Success to me means building trust and guiding clients through every step of their financial journey.
Quote: I value getting to know my clients on a personal level. I use a consultative based planning approach, and like to think of myself as a financial coach that helps my clients plan for their future, but also educates and empowers them to make confident financial decisions. My goal is always to put my clients in the best possible position for long-term success.
Service description 1: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Service eyebrow 2: DREAMS INTO ACTIONABLE PLANS

Service description 3: We recognize the unique challenges and opportunities executives encounter. Our goal is to help you develop a strategy that simplifies the complexity of managing wealth while balancing the demands of your role.
Full description:
Eric grew up in Northern New Jersey, surrounded by his family of artists, musicians, and designers. This creative environment deeply influenced his approach to wealth management, allowing him to think outside the box when developing financial strategies.

His passion for education is central to his career. He has mentored many advisors throughout the years, helping them build successful careers in wealth management. He has also taught adult finance classes and often speaks at community events, sharing the importance of financial education. He believes understanding your finances is essential to making informed decisions for the future.

At the heart of his work is a commitment to helping clients create, implement, and manage their financial goals. Whether it's debt management, retirement planning, tax-efficient strategies, or estate planning, he provides personalized, holistic advice. He often works across generations, helping families establish long-term financial security.

Eric lives in Denville, New Jersey with his wife and has two children. They are actively engaged in their local community, supporting animal shelters, food banks, and organizations such as the Red Cross, as well as local churches and synagogues.

Name: Erin Niehaus
Intro description: My 25-year career across top institutional investment firms, RIAs and a global private bank has centered on optimizing financial plans for sophisticated investors and ultra-high-net-worth families—complex portfolios, major liquidity events, and strategies built to span generations. I recently created a proprietary program for planning for aging parents, filling an unmet need I saw from my clients’ experiences. Today, I bring that institutional-grade rigor to the real-world challenges individuals and families actually face—the Great Wealth Transfer and intergenerational planning,  career changes, divorce, the loss of a spouse—pairing the technical depth to solve them with the lived experience to understand them. As a CFP®, I focus on tax-optimized, cost-efficient portfolios grounded in planning for liquidity today, lifestyle for the years ahead, and legacy for the people who matter most.
Quote: My superpower lies in simplifying financial discussions, making planning and investing both manageable and solution-oriented, and effectively communicating these concepts to all stakeholders.
Service eyebrow 1: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 1: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to each client’s specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation, along with current economic data, to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Service eyebrow 2: DIVERSIFICATION AND INNOVATION IN PORTFOLIOS
Service description 2: We actively research alternative investment opportunities and monitor your portfolio investment holdings, bringing together actionable insights and forward-thinking risk assessments.
Service description 3: Empower women by breaking down barriers they encounter in financial management. Equip them with strategies to navigate financial challenges during life's curveballs, such as divorce or the loss of a family member.
Full description:
Erin Niehaus joins Savvy Advisors after her tenure at JPMorgan, where she specialized in the Private Bank, providing comprehensive financial planning, banking, liquidity management, and investment strategies for venture capital and private equity funds and their partners. Before her time at JPMorgan, Erin worked at Bordeaux Wealth Advisors, a Barron's Top 100 Advisory firm based in Menlo Park.

She began her career as an equity research analyst at Jennison Associates Capital Corp, managing a $150 billion pension fund in New York. Subsequently, she transitioned to Silicon Valley to help establish Bowman Capital, a $4 billion hedge fund focused on high-tech investments. She served as a portfolio manager and led stock research in semiconductors and wireless technologies.

Erin continued her journey as a portfolio manager at RS Investments in the Growth Equity group, before embarking on her entrepreneurial path as head of strategy and growth for two startups. She graduated from Georgetown University as a Baker Scholar and earned her MBA from the Stern School at New York University.

An accomplished professional, Erin is a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™, a Certified Exit Planner (CEPA), and holds the Series 65 license. Additionally, she is a licensed insurance broker.

Since beginning my career as a financial analyst, I quickly developed a passion for helping clients holistically plan and improve their financial futures. From portfolio risk management to tax avoidance strategies, I provide thoughtful advice aimed at helping my clients achieve lasting financial independence.

Eugene Hoover is immensely passionate about the markets and financial literacy. While earning a Bachelor of Science in Economics from the University of Nevada, Reno, he found purpose and enjoyment in swing trading securities.

Outside of the financial world, he’s a staunch believer in the outdoors. His favorite activities include fishing and exploring the wilderness.

Name: Evan Melching
Intro description: Hello there! I’m Evan Melching, a Wealth Manager and AWMA™️ from Indianapolis, Indiana, specializing in financial planning, tax-saving strategies, and retirement planning. With nearly a decade of experience as a financial advisor, I’m passionate about crafting financial plans that are as unique as the person behind them. With a deep understanding of market trends, risk management, and long-term investment strategies, I empower my clients to make confidently informed decisions.
Quote: I believe financial success isn’t just about numbers. It’s about understanding your personal goals, lifestyle, and values.
Service eyebrow 1: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 1: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 2: UNDERSTAND YOUR INCOME STREAMS
Service description 2: Understand your income with an annual plan showing where cash flow is generated, and why. This weaves together Restricted Stock Units (RSU) flows, stock option exercises, long-term capital gains, Roth Conversions, etc.
Service description 3: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Full description:
Evan Melching is an Accredited Wealth Management Advisor™️ from Indianapolis, Indiana. While Evan has spent nearly a decade as a financial advisor, his initial career plan was to coach or teach. However, the resulting hardships his family faced from the 2008 recession changed everything. From that moment, Evan started reading about economics, investing, psychology, and risk. He saw that money wasn’t just about numbers—it was health, marriages, dreams, and peace of mind.

Evan began his career as a financial advisor at Merrill Lynch in 2017. He slowly began building his expertise across financial planning, estate and legacy planning, portfolio construction, wealth management, tax-efficient strategies, stock options, retirement planning, cash flow and supplemental income, and insurance. Today, he’s proud to empower families in making informed decisions about their future.

Outside of helping families navigate financial matters, he loves spending time with family, weightlifting, and bow hunting. His greatest loves in life are his two perfect kids and his beautiful wife.
Faq answer 1:
A friend of my family, lost nearly everything in 2008. He had a business, a house, two kids in college, and a retirement fund he’d been building for 25 years. Then came the crash. No diversification, no guidance, and no one to tell him to pull the reins when the market started shaking.

I remember he told me, with tears in his eyes, “I thought I had a plan. I really did.”

I was just about to graduate from high school then, and not sure what I was going to study in college. But that moment stuck with me. I started reading everything from economics to investing to psychology and risk. I saw that money wasn’t just numbers—it was health, marriages, dreams, and peace of mind. I saw that most people don’t have a plan. And even when they do, they don’t have someone in their corner when the punches come.

I had found my passion. I became obsessed with learning everything I could about building resilience beyond portfolios. I learned how to communicate hard truths, listen when people were scared, and how to stay steady when the market wasn’t. That discipline became my north star. I officially began my financial career in 2017 at Merrill Lynch.
Faq answer 2: I work with a diverse array of clients, spanning young professionals, small business owners, C-suite executives, and retirees.
Faq answer 4: I primarily help clients with income planning, growth, tax efficiency, and cash management strategies.
Faq answer 5: Ultimately, my favorite thing is helping clients reach their goals. I also love taking the edge off of their financial concerns. I aim to serve as a sounding board for clarity, comfort, and stability in times of uncertainty.
Faq answer 6: I love the support team, the staff, and the technology. Savvy provides the flexibility and autonomy to help clients with their specific needs.The culture, collaboration, and excitement the team has about what we do, I’ve never experienced anything like it.

Intro description:
Hello there! 👋🏼 I'm Frank, a highly experienced industry professional with over 10 years of expertise. As a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ and IRS Enrolled Agent (EA), I possess the knowledge and skills to guide individuals, families, and small businesses through the intricate landscape of taxes and investments.

When it comes to financial management, I believe in tailoring my approach to meet each individual's unique needs and aspirations. Whether you're embarking on your career journey or planning for retirement, my dedication lies in assisting you in making well-informed decisions that align with your financial goals.
Quote: I love helping build custom financial plans for clients to achieve their goals in the short and long term. I help them plan for traveling the world and for those emergency expenses in a tax-efficient way.

Full description:
As a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ professional and an Enrolled Agent authorized to represent taxpayers before the Internal Revenue Service, Frank provides tax guidance to clients as part of his advisory relationship. Frank Remund grew up in southwest Washington as the youngest of three children in a highly competitive family. From a young age, he learned that knowledge, planning, and hard work are the keys to success and that listening is crucial.

Frank's interest in investing was kindled as a child when he was gifted a few shares of stock. This initial curiosity has since matured into a lifelong passion. After graduating from high school, Frank was accepted into the University of Washington. There, he pursued his Bachelor of Science degree in Economics while also competing on the Huskies’ track and field team as a high jumper and serving as the team captain. The fundamental lessons that Frank learned during his upbringing have been instrumental throughout his professional journey. They have enabled him to establish strong, personal relationships with his clients, understand their priorities, and develop personalized financial plans that secure their financial success.

Frank has had the privilege of teaching the rigorous Retirement Income tax course for H&R Block tax professionals, as well as courses on Employee Stock Plan Compensation, Restricted Stock Units, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and Non-Qualified Options.

Frank now joins Savvy Advisors, bringing his wealth of experience and passion for financial planning. He resides in Boise, Idaho, with his wife Abby, and their four very active school-age boys. In his spare time, he enjoys volunteering as a coach for their baseball, soccer, and basketball teams. Frank's life is enriched by family, church, and work, and he considers himself very fortunate.

Name: Gabe Boruff
Intro description:
Hi 👋🏼 I’m Gabe. I’m a financial advisor based in the Tri-Cities, Washington, and I work with individuals, families, high-net-worth clients, and small business owners on financial planning, retirement planning, investment management, and other important financial decisions.

My background as a collegiate and professional baseball player and later as a collegiate coach continues to shape how I work with clients today. Coaching taught me to listen closely, understand someone’s goals, create a plan, and provide steady guidance along the way. I bring that same relationship-focused approach to financial planning, with an emphasis on clear communication and service.
Quote: I focus on getting to know my clients, understanding what matters to them, and creating a financial plan that reflects their needs and goals. My background in coaching influences how I communicate, guide, and support clients throughout the process.
Service description 1: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Service eyebrow 2: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 2: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 3: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 3: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to each client’s specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Service description 4: We actively research alternative investment opportunities and monitor your portfolio investment holdings, bringing together actionable insights and forward-thinking risk assessments.
Full description:
Gabe Boruff brings a background in athletics, coaching, and financial services to his work with clients. Before focusing his career on financial advice, Gabe played collegiate and professional baseball through his mid-20s. He then spent more than a decade coaching baseball at the collegiate level.

While coaching, Gabe also worked alongside his father as a financial consultant. That experience introduced him to financial services and gave him an opportunity to see how thoughtful guidance could make a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

After the birth of his third child, Gabe wanted a career that would allow him to spend more time at home with his family. He transitioned back into financial services and became a financial advisor at Edward Jones. In 2019, he joined Integrity Financial, where he spent the following years working alongside other advisors and continuing to develop his planning approach.

Gabe credits his baseball background with shaping many of the values he brings to his practice. Playing taught him the importance of discipline, persistence, and preparation. Coaching taught him how important strong relationships, communication, and trust are when helping someone work toward a goal. Today, he brings those lessons into each client relationship.

Gabe has lived in the Tri-Cities, Washington, since 2013 with his wife, Erika, a second-grade teacher, and their three children. Outside of work, family remains an important part of his life, and he enjoys supporting his children in their academics, sports, and music.
Faq answer 1:
My path into financial services started while I was coaching collegiate baseball. I needed additional income at the time, so I began working alongside my father as a financial consultant at his agency.

After my third child was born, I wanted to be home more and have greater flexibility to be present for my family. That led me back into financial services full time, and I became a financial advisor at Edward Jones. In 2019, I joined Integrity Financial, where I had the opportunity to work at a boutique practice alongside talented advisors who helped me continue developing my skills and approach.

My experience as both a player and a coach still influences the way I work today. I learned the importance of preparation, discipline, communication, and building relationships, and I bring those principles into my work with clients.
Faq answer 2: I work with high-net-worth clients, small business owners, families, and individuals. While each client’s financial situation is different, I enjoy working with people who value a personal relationship with their advisor and want thoughtful guidance as they make financial decisions.
Faq answer 3:
My primary areas of focus include financial and retirement planning, business retirement plan management and strategies, investment management, and life insurance planning.

I also work with clients who are considering real estate exchange strategies, including 1031 exchanges, 721 exchanges, and Delaware Statutory Trusts, depending on their circumstances and planning needs.
Faq answer 4:
I often help clients develop financial planning and retirement strategies based on their individual goals. For business owners, that may include retirement plan management and planning. I also work with clients on investment strategies, life insurance and annuity considerations, and certain real estate exchange strategies.

The starting point is understanding what the client is trying to accomplish. From there, I work to organize the different pieces of their financial life into a plan they can understand and follow.
Faq answer 5:
I really enjoy getting to know my clients and their families. Over time, those relationships give me a deeper understanding of what matters to them and what they are working toward.

It is rewarding to provide guidance and motivation as clients make progress toward their financial goals. For me, the relationship is an important part of the work, not just the plan itself.
Faq answer 6:
What stood out to me from day one was the depth of support available through Savvy. I have access to people who can assist with client onboarding, technology implementation, investment strategies, retirement plans, and marketing, which allows me to spend more of my time focused on clients.

I also appreciate having integrated technology available to both advisors and clients, along with access to a range of investment strategies and resources that can support the planning process. The combination of technology, investment resources, and operational support gives me additional tools to serve clients while continuing to build my practice.

Name: Gary Jones
Intro description:
Hi, I'm Gary Jones. I'm a financial advisor based in Lee's Summit, Missouri, with 18 years of experience helping clients plan for retirement, manage their investments, and prepare for important financial transitions.

I believe good financial planning starts with getting to know the person behind the numbers. I take the time to understand what motivates each client, what they want their future to look like, and what matters most to them. From there, we can build a plan together, put it into action, and revisit it as life and priorities change.
Quote: I take the time to understand what matters most to each client, then build a plan around their goals and adjust it as life changes.
Team description:
The prairie has always represented something meaningful to us. It is wide open, full of possibility, and allows you to see a long way down the road. The oak, on the other hand, is deeply rooted. It grows slowly and steadily, stands strong through changing seasons, and provides shelter for generations.

That combination feels a lot like what we believe good financial advice should be.

A strong foundation. A clear view of what lies ahead. The flexibility to adapt when life changes. And the patience to grow something that can last for generations.

Our goal has never been to tell our clients what their financial lives should look like. It is to listen—to understand what matters most to them—and then help them build a plan that gives them the confidence and freedom to pursue it.

For some, that may mean creating the freedom to retire. For others, it may mean caring for family, building a legacy, giving generously, or simply having the confidence to know they are on the right path.

Whatever your goals may be, we believe you deserve a financial advisor who knows your story, understands where you want to go, and is willing to walk alongside you for the journey.

Service eyebrow 2: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS

Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Service description 3: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Service description 4: Building a successful business is an incredible feat, but what happens to your hard-earned legacy when you're ready to step down? We build strategic blueprints to help ensure the continued growth and success of your enterprise.
Full description:
Gary Jones is a financial advisor with 18 years of experience helping clients work through retirement planning, investment management, portfolio construction, tax considerations, and business and farm succession planning.

His interest in investing began well before he became an advisor. In the 1980s, Gary worked on the operations side of the financial industry with DST. As he began managing some of his own money, he realized that becoming a financial advisor was a natural next step and an opportunity to spend his career helping people.

Today, Gary works with a wide range of clients and believes each relationship should begin with a deeper understanding of what the client wants to accomplish. He takes time to learn about their priorities and motivations before developing a financial plan and investment strategy around their individual circumstances.

Gary also believes financial topics do not need to feel overwhelming. A central part of his work is helping clients understand complex decisions in straightforward terms so they can stay engaged with their plan. As life changes, Gary meets with clients to review their progress and determine whether their financial plan should change with it.

Faq answer 2: I work with all types of clients because financial goals look different for everyone. My job is to dig deeper than the numbers and understand what each person truly wants to accomplish. Once I understand their priorities and what motivates them, we can work together on a plan built around those goals.
Faq answer 3: My work includes retirement planning, business and farm succession planning, investment management, portfolio construction and implementation, and tax-aware planning. These areas often overlap, so I look at how the different pieces of a client's financial life work together.
Faq answer 4: I help clients with investment and planning strategies ranging from straightforward needs to more complex situations. Every client is different, so I start by understanding the need rather than beginning with a predetermined strategy. From there, we can develop an approach that fits the client's circumstances and long-term goals.
Faq answer 5: I love getting to know my clients, learning about their goals, and helping them work toward what matters to them. Finances can feel overwhelming, so I enjoy taking complicated topics and making them easier to understand. At the end of the day, I got into this business because I wanted to help people.

I came into this business because I wanted to help people, so it is valuable to have a team behind me that approaches the work with that same mindset.

Full description:
George Rabon, CFP®, AIF®, is a financial advisor with 12 years of experience working with successful families, business owners, physicians, dentists, pre-retirees, and retirees. His work centers on bringing together financial planning, investment management, retirement planning and tax considerations based on each client’s circumstances and priorities.

George’s path into wealth management began in public accounting. He earned a B.S. in Accounting from Clemson University, where he was a member of the Clemson football team, and later earned his Master’s degree in Accounting from the College of Charleston with a focus in Taxation. He is also a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ professional and an Accredited Investment Fiduciary®.

His accounting background provides an important perspective when evaluating how investment and planning decisions may affect a client’s broader tax picture.George likes to work alongside clients’ CPAs, attorneys, and other professional advisors to coordinate different areas of their financial lives.

George lives in Summerville, South Carolina, with his wife and three children. His Christian faith is an important part of his life and shapes his view of stewardship and serving others. Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his family, volunteering at church, playing golf with friends and bow hunting in the outdoors.

For George, wealth management is about helping clients bring greater clarity and intentionality to the resources they have built, while keeping their families, priorities, and long-term goals at the center of the planning process.

Name: Gunnar Johnson
Intro description:
Hi 👋🏼 I’m Gunnar. I work with families and business owners who want their financial decisions to reflect what matters most to them. For many of my clients, that includes thinking intentionally about stewardship, generosity, and the purpose behind their wealth.

My background in financial counseling, business ownership, ministry, and charitable planning shapes how I approach investment management and financial planning. At True Harvest Private Wealth, I help clients connect their resources with their values and long-term goals.
Quote: I enjoy getting to know people on a deep and personal level, understanding what matters most to them, and helping them make thoughtful decisions about how they earn, manage, and give their resources.
Team description:
At True Harvest Private Wealth, we believe wealth is most meaningful when it is managed with intention and connected to the people, values, and causes that matter most. Our team works collaboratively with business owners, families, and charitably minded clients to bring greater clarity and purpose to complex financial decisions.

Our approach brings together investment management, charitable giving strategies, business transition planning, and estate planning to help clients see the bigger picture. Whether preparing for a business transition, planning for future generations, or exploring ways to make a greater charitable impact, we help clients thoughtfully steward what they have built while planning for what comes next.
Service description 1: Whether it’s transferring assets to kids or grandkids, or maximizing your charitable donations, we have the expertise with complex strategies surrounding wealth transfer.
Service eyebrow 2: DREAMS INTO ACTIONABLE PLANS
Service description 2: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Service eyebrow 3: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 3: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Full description:
Gunnar Johnson is a wealth manager, business owner, nonprofit leader, investor, and consultant who works with business owners and families seeking to manage their wealth with greater purpose. His perspective has been shaped by decades spent at the intersection of financial stewardship, ministry, business ownership, and charitable planning.

Gunnar’s path began in 1999 with Crown Financial Ministries, where his work in biblical financial counseling laid the foundation for a career centered on the relationship between faith and finances. He later became a budget coach and worked alongside churches to help individuals and families think intentionally about money and possessions. In 2004, Ron Blue invited Gunnar to help build what became Kingdom Advisors, and Gunnar completed the Certified Kingdom Advisor® training in 2006.

His work has continued across ministry, nonprofit leadership, consulting, and entrepreneurship. Gunnar served for 11 years as an executive pastor and spent 12 years as a board member or president of the Christian Stewardship Network. He also spent 15 years serving alongside Israel Firstfruits, supporting entrepreneurship and economic development in Israel. As the owner of five businesses himself, Gunnar understands both the challenges and the rewards that can come with building and leading a company.

Over the years, Gunnar saw a recurring challenge. Generous people wanted to support causes close to their hearts, but the complexities of business ownership, financial planning, and charitable decisions could make it difficult to know how and when to act. That experience ultimately led him into wealth management and to True Harvest Private Wealth.

Today, Gunnar helps families and business owners think through investment planning, strategic spending, charitable goals, and the broader purpose behind their wealth. For clients who share his Christian worldview, that can include conversations about the theology of money and possessions and what faithful stewardship looks like in practice.

That commitment to generosity extends beyond Gunnar’s work with clients. He is involved with Dream Centers, an organization serving vulnerable women and children in Colorado Springs.

Outside of work, Gunnar enjoys exploring Colorado by motorcycle and on skis. He and his wife, Missy, especially enjoy spending time with their granddaughter, Charlie.

We build a comprehensive financial plan that connects every piece, tax, investments, estate, cash flow, so you can see exactly where you are, where you are going, and what you need to do next.
Service description 3: RSUs. Stock options. Deferred comp. Executive benefits packages were not designed to be simple and most people accept them without fully understanding what they have. We break down exactly what you own, when it vests, what it is worth, and how to make the most of it without a surprise tax bill. You negotiated hard for this compensation. Let's make sure you actually keep it.
Service eyebrow 4: BUILT FOR THE WAY YOU ACTUALLY LIVE
Service description 4: Women outlive men, take more career pauses, and still retire with significantly less. That is not a mindset problem. It is a planning problem. We build investment strategies that account for your real timeline, your real income trajectory, and the real moments - maternity leaves, career pivots, business launches- that make your financial life look different from the standard model. Being different is not a disadvantage. It just requires a more comprehensive and flexible plan.
Full description:
Hannah Basil Bryant, CFP® is a Chicago-based financial planner with 11 years of experience helping professional women and families build wealth with intention.

Her path into financial planning began at her first job in commercial banking, where she noticed that colleagues with the same salary and starting point were making very different financial decisions. Because her mother was a financial planner, Hannah understood the value of early planning and compound interest. She wanted to help close that knowledge gap for people who did not have the same advantage.

In 2015, Hannah joined her mother, Lois Basil, at Basil Financial Group, where she helped organize and expand the business while building services for younger clients. Together, they grew the practice to over $75M in AUM before its acquisition in 2023. Today, Hannah is building her next chapter as an independent financial planner and founder of Ambitious and Aligned, a wealth and coaching platform for women navigating career and life transitions.

Hannah is a contributing voice in Neha Ruch’s The Power Pause, a founding member of the Power Pause Community, and a founding member of Grand Pursuit, a community for entrepreneurial women in pursuit of career success and family fulfillment, not one or the other. She graduated summa cum laude in economics from Knox College and studied corporate finance and international marketing at the London School of Economics. She holds the CFP® designation, is a member of the FPA, and is a sustaining member of Phi Beta Kappa.

A lifelong Chicagoan, Hannah lives in the North Mayfair neighborhood with her husband, Caleb, their two young children, and their dog. Outside of work, she enjoys hosting dinner parties, making memories with her family, stand-up paddle boarding, and traveling.

I’m Hunter, a CPA-turned-financial advisor based in Kentucky.  After three years in public accounting, I wanted to leverage my experience and knowledge for forward planning and optimization.  I work with P&G employees and retirees, executives, business owners, and people approaching or enjoying retirement who want a simpler, more proactive plan.

By combining my tax expertise with holistic financial planning, I help clients simplify their financial life while instilling confidence in their plan moving forward.
Quote: My job is to make your financial life simpler, your plan more proactive, and your decisions more confident—by combining tax expertise with holistic planning.

Service eyebrow 3: STRATEGIC PLANNING OF YOUR FINANCIAL AND NON-FINANCIAL COMPENSATION

Full description: Hunter Cloud, CPA, CFP® is a financial advisor based in Kentucky who specializes in helping clients make confident retirement and tax-planning decisions. He began his career in public accounting, where he spent three years as a CPA, before transitioning into advising to focus on creating proactive, high-impact value for clients. His tax background allows him to concentrate on what is controllable—optimizing cash flow, reducing lifetime tax liability, and aligning financial decisions with long-term goals. Shaped in part by witnessing the financial and personal strain experienced by a close family friend during the 2008 financial crisis, Hunter takes seriously the responsibility of guiding clients through all phases of life. He believes that less is more when it comes to advice, favoring clear, concise communication and an approach rooted in listening, education, and trust.

I began my career as a CPA in public accounting, and after three years, I realized I wasn't adding the kind of value I wanted to for my clients. This inspired me to transition into an advisory role, where I could leverage my tax background to focus on the controllable aspects of a client's financial life. Intro description:
Hi 👋🏼 I'm James. For more than 20 years, I've helped individuals and families plan for their financial futures, with a particular focus on helping people prepare for retirement and navigate the years that follow.

Many of my clients have spent decades building careers, businesses, farms, and families. When retirement approaches, I help them bring the different pieces of their financial lives together through retirement planning, income planning, asset allocation, and legacy planning. I take the time to understand what matters to each client so we can build a plan around the life they want to live.
Quote: I want to get to know my clients where they are, understand what matters to them, and build a financial plan that helps them prepare for retirement and the life they want to live.

Full description:
James Soukup brings more than 20 years of financial advisory experience to his work with individuals and families. He has been a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® professional since 2014 and focuses much of his work on helping clients prepare for retirement and organize the different pieces of their financial lives.

His interest in investing began well before his professional career. James grew up on a farm in eastern Nebraska, where some of his first paychecks came from moving irrigation pipe and detasseling seed corn. At around 12 years old, James and his brother each raised a bucket calf and used some of the proceeds to buy stock. That early experience sparked an interest in investing that would eventually become his career.

James earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Nebraska at Kearney and later earned his MBA from the University of Arkansas. Over the course of his career, he has worked in both large and small financial services organizations, including full-service and discount brokerage environments.

Today, James works with individuals and families from a wide range of backgrounds and at many different stages of life, including farmers, business owners, educators and other professionals, and retirees. He takes a comprehensive approach to financial planning, helping clients navigate retirement and income planning, investment and asset allocation strategies, concentrated stock positions, tax-aware planning, and estate and legacy considerations.

Relationships are central to how James works. He takes time to understand a client's background, family, priorities, and plans for retirement. Sometimes that means meeting across a conference table. Other times, it can mean making a house call and getting to know a client over the dinner table.

James and his wife, Mikka, live in Linwood, Kansas, with their three children. Outside of work, he enjoys gardening, attending his children's sporting events, and fishing local ponds. He is also a member of Trout Unlimited.

He is a member of Backcountry Hunters and Anglers and a founding member of MoKan Trout Unlimited.

Full description:
Jeff Brimhall is a managing partner at Blue Barn Wealth, where he enjoys working with clients to simplify their life and master their finances. Prior to Blue Barn Wealth, Jeff served as a Senior Advisor at Soltis Investment Advisors and acted as interim CEO of Ampelis, a corporate and family consulting company focused on successful transitions of culture and assets between generations.

Earlier in his career, Jeff was an award-winning faculty member in Finance and Economics at Case Western Reserve University, an equity analyst in National City Bank’s Private Client Group, and held analyst and advisory roles at Lee Financial, a Registered Investment Advisor in Dallas, TX, and Crow Holdings.

Jeff earned a PhD in Economics from Southern Methodist University and a B.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering from Brigham Young University. He is a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ professional and holds the Chartered Financial Analyst designation. Jeff has also served as Chairman of the Utah Chapter of the Financial Planning Association and taught in the Personal Financial Planning Program at Utah Valley University.

After a transformative 12-year career as a global corporate retail designer, Jennifer pivoted to financial planning, driven by a profound personal loss. This experience reshaped her purpose, leading her to become a wealth manager dedicated to offering comfort, clarity, and guidance to those navigating grief—particularly in matters of money, legacy, and family division.

With seven years of experience in financial planning, formerly with Edward Jones Investments and Huntington Bank, Jenny joined Savvy Advisors to embrace its tech-forward and client-focused model. Unbound by the limitations of traditional firms, she offers her services nationwide, combining flexible in-person meetings with convenient digital and online communication options. Deep, empathetic listening drives Jenny's creative investment solutions that build lasting relationships.

Faq answer 1:
The pivot point in my career came when my best friend, Ruth, died from Colon Cancer at 32 years old.

In 2015, I had been a designer for almost 12 years. I had become an expert in corporate retail, clothing design and production, but was disillusioned by what I had seen in the Industry around the world. I had traveled around the world 18 times by then, visiting 2-5 countries each time, and saw the end coming for this untenable exploitation of cheap labor, and indiscriminately waste expulsion into rivers and streams. Then in February 2015, Ruth passed. She had been diagnosed one year prior and it started as stage 4 Colon Cancer. During that last year of Ruth's life, I was with her for first appointments, every month spending days or a week with her, to be a point of encouragement, of brevity, of witness, of support. That time, and all time after has transformed me into someone else.

I realized that when you lose your person, you never "move on", you never wake up "not thinking about them" or at least they are never far from your thoughts. Ruth was my person. My secure connection in addition to my parents. We knew each other since 4th grade or so, but became and grew into each other's closest person, sharing everything, always looping back together, always continuing the conversation, no matter what changed, no matter how we grew, we grew together. and then.... she was gone.

Grieving like this has shown me that there is such an incredible need for comfort in loss. Through my years of grief, I have been witness to additional grief over money and THINGS. Division of families, which would have never been the intention of the dead. Intentions not known! When in pain, deep pain and grief, people most times are not their best selves. May I bring peace, compassion and guidance to all those suffering. May we all know that we all suffer. I was left questioning: how do I keep living? and the answer was to say YES, to a new experience.

Thorough evaluation of my past skills, and new experiences, lead me to seeking deeply the next thing. I had a trusted Financial Advisor, who I had seen for years, and she suggested I do what she does. So, I did. A year later, after extensive training and testing, I started serving clients. I immediately saw the need for my work and the impact and importance.

I came to Savvy Advisors after working with Edward Jones Investments and with Huntington Bank, after looking for a more functional, intentional, tech based investment adviser.

Now, I offer clients a better experience, with less of the entanglements of a traditional financial company. A forward thinking, diverse, savvy company, I'm happy to have the support of this company to build my intentional practice.

Even highly successful law firm partners make avoidable financial mistakes — not because they lack intelligence, but because their income is complex, their time is limited, and their advice is often fragmented.

From underutilized 401(k) brokerage link options to missed tax strategies and uncoordinated planning, these gaps can quietly cost you millions over time.

Inside the playbook, you'll get the frameworks to:

  • Build a 3-bucket cash-flow system that turns volatile draws into a predictable plan
  • Nail quarterly estimates and safe harbor — without overpaying the IRS an interest-free loan
  • Survive your lateral year, from capital contributions to the first-draw gap
  • Handle capital calls as a routine transaction, not a financial crisis
  • Optimize your 401(k), BrokerageLink, and private-market access to cut unnecessary taxes
  • Design a retirement paycheck from partner wealth — with a clear number and a clear date

Faq answer 1:
Earlier in my career, I worked as a Trusts & Estates (T&E) attorney, advising ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals. This led me to an introduction to Allen & Company’s Wealth Management division, where the focus was on providing financial advice and tax guidance to UHNW families and institutional investors. Initially, Allen & Company sought to bring me in to focus exclusively on T&E planning for their clients, but I expressed an interest in offering both T&E advice and financial guidance. They supported this ambition, in part because of my background in finance and accounting, which I studied during my undergraduate years, as well as my experience working at Wharton while attending the University of Pennsylvania Law School.

At Allen & Company, I earned the Chartered Financial Analyst® designation and worked closely with families and institutions on strategic and tactical asset allocation opportunities, tax guidance, and succession planning. My expertise spans a few key areas that include tax and succession planning, concentrated position management, behavioral coaching, evidence-based portfolio management, sourcing alternative investments, and family communication.

Tax and Legacy Planning - I was a practicing attorney and spent most of my legal career working with families to help them achieve their business and succession planning objectives in a structure that maximized their wealth, net of income, gift, and estate taxes.

Concentrated Position Management - I have significant experience guiding clients with respect to concentrated equity positions, including analyzing risk, income tax and transfer tax considerations.  I’ve helped CEOs and board members of public companies craft 10b5-1 selling plans to systematically reduce their exposure to concentrated holdings.

Behavioral Coaching - In my decade-plus of working with clients, I have learned that the best plan is one that the client can stick with through good times and bad.

Research-Based Portfolio Management - I believe in the importance of using data to set the baseline for decision making and for projecting ranges of outcomes. This means that I lean on academic and practitioner research to inform my views and recommendations rather than the latest short-term narrative that financial media is focusing on.

Alternative Investments - Prior to joining Savvy, I evaluated private investment opportunities on behalf of clients, with a focus on expected returns net of taxes and fees, while ensuring that my clients also preserved sufficient liquidity.

Family Communication - Finally, I believe in the importance of helping families talk effectively about their wealth so that core values can be passed to the next generation. Defining and funding a good life can mean many different things to different people, and clarifying roles and expectations can be extremely valuable when it comes to maintaining family harmony.
Faq answer 4:
The strategies are tailored to client goals, time horizon, and ability and willingness to take risks. However, there are a few foundational principles across my strategies, including a focus on tax efficiency, maintaining a long-term orientation, an emphasis on quality, constant re-underwriting of investment theses, and operating with the conviction to act opportunistically during periods of market dislocation.

Tax Efficiency: Incorporating tax planning into portfolio management includes managing “asset location.” In other words, holding high-yielding assets in tax-advantaged accounts and lower-yielding assets in taxable accounts. It also means not day-trading portfolios and therefore not generating short-term capital gains or unnecessary transaction costs where possible.

“Long-Termism”: I am a steadfast believer in the extraordinary compounding of capital that can occur after long holding periods.  In my opinion, timing the market is incredibly dangerous.  Investors need to be right twice - selling at the top and then having the courage to buy back in after a steep decline, which is often at a very scary moment in time.  It is a cliche, but for most investors, time in the market beats timing the market.

Quality: Generally, the best businesses in the world are those that:

provide a product or service that people regularly need and where there are few good substitutes

do so better, cheaper, or faster than others

do so repeatedly, and

do it without sinking a mountain of capital and fixed costs into the ground (i.e., if they are “capital-light” businesses).

These businesses tend to earn customer loyalty, utility-like usage, and pricing power that allows for sustained earnings growth and reinvestment back into the business. When I recommend external fund managers for clients, I ensure that they adhere to a similar philosophy on quality investing over long periods.

Continuous Evaluation: Having a long-term outlook does not mean “set it and forget it”. In fact, holding investments for long periods of time should be the opposite of set it and forget it. I believe that long-term holds require a constant sense of paranoia that the investment thesis is wrong: this healthy paranoia forces difficult questions and encourages more thought and circumspection throughout the life of an investment.

Strategic and Tactical Opportunism: Crises and dislocations are natural phenomena in the markets, almost purge-like episodes following periods of relative calm. Finding clarity and conviction in these moments is difficult—plenty of capital managers have been found hiding in their caves during crises—but if an investor can successfully identify and capitalize on a dislocation, they may be rewarded over long periods of time. I plan to approach each and every day—and every crisis—with a prepared mind, and I believe my clients will be well-suited to react to these opportunities with conviction as a result.

I derive great personal satisfaction in seeing my clients achieve their goals, whether it is buying a home, fully funding their retirement, paying for a dream vacation, or enabling their child to go to the school that seemed out of reach.

Ultimately, I want my clients to feel safer and feel that they can offload their financial and life stressors to me, which is a responsibility I embrace.

Name: Joshua Joffe
Intro description:
Hi, I’m Josh. I work with individuals and families who want a clear plan and a steady partner when financial decisions start to feel heavy.

A lot of people think this work is about picking the right investments. Investing matters, but much of the real value shows up in the day-to-day questions that inform the investment decisions themselves. Questions like: Can I retire sooner than I thought? What should I do with my equity compensation? How do I balance saving, giving, and enjoying life without feeling like I’m making a mistake?

My job is to help you get organized, make sound decisions with the information we actually have, and stay disciplined when the noise gets loud.
Quote: My goal is to understand you. In every conversation, I try to put myself in your shoes. I may not have lived your exact experience, but I want to understand the thoughts, fears, and decisions you’re facing. Based on that understanding, I’ll work with you to provide clarity.
Service eyebrow 1: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 1: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to your specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Service eyebrow 2: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 2: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service description 3: We actively research alternative investment opportunities and monitor your portfolio investment holdings, bringing together actionable insights and forward-thinking risk assessments.
Service description 4: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible, ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Full description:
While Josh’s career in wealth management now spans over 20 years, he often jokes that he’s an accidental advisor. With a non-traditional background, his introduction to capital markets happened shortly after college, when he began his career as an equities trader. That experience sparked a deeper interest and passion for investing, and led him into private client portfolio management.

Josh later joined a leading global asset management firm, where he served in senior portfolio management roles. His early years coincided with the 2008 financial crisis, giving him firsthand exposure to risk, market stress, and the importance of discipline. That period shaped how he thinks about portfolio construction and long-term planning.

Over time, he realized he wanted to be closer to the people behind the portfolios. He earned his MBA while working full time and later obtained his CFP® certification. He then joined an independent wealth management firm, where he began engaging directly in financial planning alongside portfolio management.

Today, Josh works with a select group of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth households, including business owners, executives, professionals, and families navigating liquidity events, concentrated equity exposure, retirement transitions, and multi-generational planning.

Josh is an inaugural member of the Nasdaq Advisor Council, where he provides perspective on portfolio strategies and industry innovation. He has been recognized among etf.com’s Top 100 Financial Advisors. Josh also serves as co-Chair of the Investment Committee at JKHA, the school his children attend.

Josh resides in Livingston, New Jersey, with his wife and two children. Outside of work, he volunteers as an EMT when time allows. Most of his free time, however, is spent with his family. He is deeply involved in his community and his children’s lives – balancing extra-curricular activities, sporting events, dance recitals, and more. Those moments are reminders that financial planning is ultimately about supporting the lives happening outside of a spreadsheet.

I try to connect these areas while helping clients think through complex financial decisions in a structured way, because in real life, they are all interconnected.

Full description:
Katherine Fibiger brings more than two decades of experience helping clients navigate the transition into retirement. Her work focuses on designing income strategies that support long-term lifestyle needs while carefully considering taxes, market conditions, and evolving priorities.

She was drawn to financial planning early on through her love of analysis and teaching. Today, she blends those strengths by helping clients understand not just what decisions to make, but why those decisions matter within the bigger picture.

Katherine specializes in retirement income planning, tax-aware strategies such as Roth conversions and withdrawal sequencing, and coordinating decisions across investments, healthcare, and legacy considerations. She values building long-term relationships and takes pride in guiding clients through one of the most important financial transitions of their lives with care and attention.

Full description:
Keith Hamberg is a Certified Financial Planner™ based in Cincinnati, OH, with more than a decade of experience helping clients navigate taxes, retirement planning, and comprehensive financial strategies. He focuses on translating complex financial topics into practical, understandable steps, allowing clients to feel organized and informed as they make important financial decisions.

Keith’s approach is centered on clarity, simplicity, and collaboration. He works closely with individuals and families to align strategies around their unique goals, whether that involves retirement planning, investment management, tax optimization, or estate and trust planning.

Outside of work, Keith is a husband and father of two. He enjoys spending time with his family, exploring Cincinnati, and keeping up with the busy, fun pace of family life.
Faq answer 1: I became a financial advisor because I understand how stressful money can be and how important it is to make thoughtful choices. Growing up in a big family and balancing work while in college taught me the value of planning ahead and understanding the consequences of decisions. Now, I work with families and individuals to help them organize their finances, feel more confident, and enjoy the life they’ve worked for.
Faq answer 2: I work with people who have spent years building their careers and providing for their families. My clients are often seeking guidance to make sense of their finances, feel in control, and plan for the future they want. Whether it’s retirement planning, investment management, or just gaining clarity over day-to-day finances, I help families feel secure and supported.
Faq answer 3: I specialize in helping clients approaching retirement navigate complex financial decisions, including managing taxes, investments, and portfolio-based income planning. My work blends growth, risk management, and long-term planning, all centered on clients’ personal goals. The aim is to provide clarity and structure so clients feel informed and prepared for the next chapter of their lives.
Faq answer 4: Every client is unique, so the strategies I employ are tailored to individual goals and circumstances. For some, the focus is on building and protecting investments to support retirement. For others, it’s planning a legacy for family or supporting charitable causes. Taxes, income planning, and risk management all play a role, and my approach is to integrate these elements in a way that reflects what matters most to each client.
Faq answer 5: The moments when it all comes together are my favorite. Whether it’s turning in a retirement notice, checking off a long-term goal, or simply enjoying time with family without financial stress, those milestones make the planning process worthwhile. Seeing clients experience those moments is incredibly rewarding.

Name: Ken Bobadilla
Intro description:
Hello 👋🏼 I’m Ken. I help retirees, families, and small business owners plan for the future with clarity and confidence. With nearly three decades of experience in financial services, I focus on estate planning, retirement planning, and business exit strategies, but above all helping clients make informed decisions that help protect what they’ve built and ensure their legacy is carried out with care.

My approach is deeply personal and educational. I take time to understand each client’s goals, family dynamics, and long-term vision, then design customized strategies for everything from structuring trusts to transitioning a business. I believe in empowering clients to enjoy what they’ve earned and preserve what they’ve saved for the next generation.
Quote: My goal is simple: help clients enjoy what they’ve earned and protect what they’ve built, so their money supports both their life today and their legacy tomorrow.
Service description 1: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Service eyebrow 2: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE

Service eyebrow 3: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN

Full description:
Ken brings nearly three decades of experience in financial services, specializing in estate planning, retirement strategies, and business exit planning. He works primarily with retirees, families, and small business owners, helping them navigate major life transitions and build plans that reflect their goals and values.

Before becoming a financial advisor, Ken spent 25 years as a professional sailor and business owner, operating a successful boat rental business in Hawaii and San Diego. That experience taught him the importance of independence, discipline, and long-term planning—principles he now applies to his work with clients every day.

Ken takes an educational, relationship-driven approach to financial planning. He helps clients design customized strategies for estate transitions, business exits, and legacy planning, with a special focus on family dynamics and trust structures. His philosophy is simple: help people enjoy what they’ve earned and thoughtfully pass on what they’ve saved.

Ken resides with his wife, who works professionally in trust management, giving him an even deeper perspective on estate and legacy planning. When he’s not working with clients, he enjoys being on the water, reflecting his lifelong connection to sailing and adventure.
Faq answer 1:
I’ve always had an analytical mind—math came naturally, and managing finances felt intuitive from an early age. But my path to financial advising wasn’t a straight line. I began my career with a science degree from San Diego State University and spent 25 years in the boating and hospitality industry, running a boat rental business and sailing professionally across Hawaii and San Diego.

When I started a family, I wanted a career that allowed me to be more present while still using my problem-solving skills and love for helping people. That’s when I discovered financial planning—it combined the analytical side of finance with the human side of making a difference in people’s lives.

Over the past 27 years, I’ve built deep expertise in estate and retirement planning through roles at firms like MassMutual, LPL, and Epstein & White. My journey has come full circle at Savvy, where I’ve returned to an independent platform that allows me to serve clients the way I believe is best: with transparency, flexibility, and genuine care.
Faq answer 2: I primarily work with retirees and small business owners—people who have worked hard to build their wealth and want to ensure it supports the next chapter of their lives. Many of my clients are navigating the transition from earning an income to living off their savings, and I help them create sustainable strategies that provide security and confidence. I also work with the next generation—the children of existing clients—helping them establish strong financial foundations early on.
Faq answer 3: My core areas of expertise include estate planning, retirement planning, and helping small business owners design thoughtful exit strategies. Over the years, I’ve developed a particular strength in estate mediation—helping families navigate complex dynamics and find common ground when planning for the future. I also have deep experience with business transitions, including structuring exits that align with both financial goals and family needs. Additionally, I often assist with the creation and coordination of trusts, including special needs trusts, drawing on both my professional experience and my family’s hands-on involvement in trust management.
Faq answer 4: I help clients with strategies that bring structure and clarity to complex transitions, whether that’s designing a business exit plan, navigating estate issues, or managing family dynamics around inheritance. A lot of my work involves helping parents plan thoughtfully when they have children with different financial habits, the most common we see are the saver, spender, or “wild card.” My goal is to create estate and transition strategies that protect family wealth while helping preserve relationships and ensuring everyone is cared for in the way that fits their needs.
Faq answer 5: My favorite part about working with clients is the opportunity to educate—to help them truly understand their options and make informed choices. I enjoy working with clients who are open to learning and value thoughtful planning. Guiding them through what’s possible (and what’s not) creates those “aha” moments that make the work deeply rewarding.
Faq answer 6: Working with Savvy has been a great fit because of the people—the team is enthusiastic, responsive, and genuinely supportive. They encourage collaboration while giving me the independence to run my practice the way I believe best serves my clients. It’s the perfect balance of freedom and partnership.

Full description:
Kevin Beutel, MBA, is a dedicated Wealth Manager in Albany, NY. His passion for financial guidance was sparked while working as a controller for an excavating company. Volunteering to teach a financial literacy course for a local nonprofit revealed his deep satisfaction in educating others and helping them achieve their next financial milestones.

Inspired by this experience, and having witnessed the significant financial challenges and lack of professional guidance faced by the blue-collar workers at the excavating company during the 2008 financial crisis, Kevin launched his career as a financial advisor. He subsequently returned to school to earn an MBA with a Master’s Level Certificate in Financial Planning.

Early in his career, he also assisted several federal clients with their taxes, which motivated him to specialize in navigating the complexities of federal benefits.

In 2025, Kevin joined Savvy. He was drawn to the firm's technology, which allows him to streamline administrative tasks and dedicate more personal time to assisting clients. Outside the office, Kevin enjoys the natural beauty of Upstate New York through activities like woodworking, gardening, hiking, and occasional kayaking with his wife.

Through this experience, I discovered my passion for teaching and helping students take their next steps. This inspired me to return to school, where I earned an MBA with a Master’s Level Certificate in Financial Planning.

In 2008, I witnessed firsthand the financial challenges and lack of guidance faced by blue-collar workers at the excavating company. These early experiences launched my career in financial advisory and fueled my commitment to helping others.

I help clients break down these complex systems into simple, understandable concepts.
Faq answer 4: I focus on financial planning, tax optimization, and retirement planning strategies for my clients.
